Remove completed and cancelled pipeline instances; failed ones only when asked. administrators only · changes things pipeline-prune [-s <string>] [--all] [--keep=<string>] [--max=<string>] [--older-than=<string>] [--budget=<string>] [<name>] Argument What it is [<name>] Pipeline name (optional; all if omitted) Option What it does -s <string> Only remove instances with this status, such as failed. --all Remove all instances, failed and running too (cancels first) --keep=<string> Retention cap: keep this many newest per pipeline, remove the rest. --max=<string> Stop after removing this many per pipeline (with --keep or --older-than) --older-than=<string> Retention by age: remove those completed longer ago than this, e.g. 30d. --budget=<string> Stop starting new pages after this long, e.g. 15m (with --keep or --older-than)

Remove pipeline instances (cancels running ones first) administrators only · changes things pipeline-remove [-f] <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID(s) Option What it does -f Ignore instances that are not found.

Return instances marked terminal while still holding unfinished steps to running. administrators only · reads only pipeline-repair [--apply] Option What it does --apply Perform the repair (default is a dry run)
Rerun pipeline(s) from the current definition, replacing the old instance. administrators only · changes things pipeline-rerun <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID(s)
Restart a failed pipeline (re-queue failed steps) administrators only · changes things pipeline-restart <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID.

Manually start a pipeline. administrators only · changes things pipeline-start [--var=<string>] <name> <path> Argument What it is <name> Pipeline name. <path> Target path to process. Option What it does --var=<string> Override a declared variable for this run: NAME=VALUE (repeatable)
Show pipeline instance status. reads only pipeline-status <id> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID.

Run one pipeline step again: a failed or skipped one, or a running one, which is stopped first. administrators only · changes things pipeline-step-restart <id> <step> Argument What it is <id> Instance ID. <step> Step name.
Remove a pipeline definition, and cancel its running instances. administrators only · changes things pipeline-undefine <name> Argument What it is <name> Pipeline name to undefine.

Run a pool worker (long-running) administrators only · changes things pipeline-worker [--pool=<path>] [--capacity=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--reserve-kind=<string>] [--reserve-capacity=<string>] [--kind-quantum=<number>] [--lease=<number>] [--name=<string>] [--concurrency=<number>] [--env=<string>] [--pass-on] [--while=<string>] [--while-every=<number>] Option What it does --pool=<path> Pool node path to claim from. --capacity=<string> Capacity offered to the pool, key=number (repeatable) --kind=<string> Only claim these job kinds (repeatable) --reserve-kind=<string> Prefer these kinds within reserved capacity (repeatable) --reserve-capacity=<string> Soft capacity reservation, key=number (repeatable) --kind-quantum=<number> Batch by kind: drain one kind for this many ms before rotating (default 0, off) --lease=<number> Lease duration in ms (default 60000) --name=<string> What pool-stat and the dashboard call this worker (default: the service it runs as) --concurrency=<number> Upper bound on concurrent jobs (default 1) --env=<string> A variable every step runs with, NAME=value (repeatable) --pass-on A step that could not run yet (exit 75) goes straight back to the pool for another worker, and its kind rests in this one. --while=<string> A command asked every --while-every seconds; the worker stops, handing its jobs back, once it fails. --while-every=<number> How often --while is asked, in seconds (default 60)
Manage work pools. pool <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

Add a job to a pool. administrators only · changes things pool-add [--kind=<string>] [--priority=<string>] [--requires=<string>] [--params=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--exclusive=<string>] [--attempts=<string>] [--delay=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --kind=<string> Capability class the job needs (required) --priority=<string> Higher runs first (default 0) --requires=<string> Resource vector, key=number (repeatable or comma-separated) --params=<string> JSON payload handed to the worker. --key=<string> Dedup key; re-adding a live one updates it instead of duplicating. --exclusive=<string> Mutex class; one claimed job per class at a time. --attempts=<string> Attempts before the job fails. --delay=<string> Hold the job back this long (e.g. 30s, 5m)

Cancel pending or claimed jobs. administrators only · changes things pool-cancel [--job=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--prefix=<string>] [--kind=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --job=<string> Cancel one job by id. --key=<string> Cancel the job with this dedup key. --prefix=<string> Cancel every job whose dedup key starts with this. --kind=<string> Cancel every job of this kind.

Claim the best matching job from a pool under a lease. administrators only · changes things pool-claim [--owner=<string>] [--offer=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--lease=<string>] [--wait] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --owner=<string> Lease owner (default derives from the session) --offer=<string> Available capacity, key=number (repeatable or comma-separated) --kind=<string> Only consider these kinds (repeatable) --lease=<string> Lease duration (default 30s) --wait Block until a job is claimable.

List jobs in a pool. reads only pool-list [--state=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--after=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --state=<string> Filter by state (comma-separated) --kind=<string> Filter by kind. --limit=<string> Page size (default 100) --after=<string> Keyset cursor from a previous page (job id)

Delete finished jobs so a pool does not grow without bound. administrators only · changes things pool-purge [--state=<string>] [--older-than=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --state=<string> States to drop (default done,failed,cancelled) --older-than=<string> Only drop jobs finished longer ago than this (e.g. 7d)

Return failed or cancelled jobs to the pool with a clean attempt count. administrators only · changes things pool-retry [--job=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--prefix=<string>] [--kind=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Pool node path. Option What it does --job=<string> Retry one job by id. --key=<string> Retry the job with this dedup key. --prefix=<string> Retry every job whose dedup key starts with this. --kind=<string> Retry every job of this kind.
Show a pool backlog, job counts, policy and throughput per job kind; every pool without a path. reads only pool-stat [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] Pool node path (default: every pool)
Try resting job kinds again now, every resting kind without a name. administrators only · changes things pool-wake [<kind>...] Argument What it is [<kind>...] Job kind to wake (repeatable)

Where nodes are: each path's name, type and the shape of its position (a location's, a picture's GPS) reads only position-get <path>... Argument What it is <path>... the nodes, or position nodes themselves. position-get /archive/locations/Exempelviken /archive/albums/Sommar/files/IMG_0001.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nodes: one per path, in order — path, name, type and position (lat, lng, and radius or polygon) when it has one; error for a path that cannot be read.

Set the shape of a position node (point, circle or polygon), making the node when it is missing. changes things position-set [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--radius=<string>] [--polygon=<string>] [--clear] <path> Argument What it is <path> path of the position node, such as /position. Option What it does --lat=<string> latitude of the center point. --lng=<string> longitude of the center point. --radius=<string> circle radius in meters. --polygon=<string> polygon ring as JSON: [{"lat":..,"lng":..},...]. --clear clear the stored shape.
Display node properties. reads only props [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links.

List the commands running now: pid, user, shell, how long, and the command line. Admin sees everyone's, anyone else their own. reads only ps [--user=<user>] Option What it does --user=<user> Only this user's commands (-u) ps ps --user anna With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One row per running command, oldest first.

List the entries a queue set aside after their delivery attempts, or retry or drop them. reads only queue-dead [--retry] [--drop] [--id=<string>] [-n <string>] [--limit=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Queue node path. Option What it does --retry put them back in line with no attempts spent. --drop delete them. --id=<string> only this entry, with --retry or --drop (repeatable) -n <string> how many entries to list (default 10) --limit=<string> how many entries to list (default 10) queue-dead /var/queues/archive-bridge queue-dead --retry /var/queues/archive-bridge queue-dead --drop -- id 42 /var/queues/archive-bridge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the dead-lettered entries: id, attempts, created, dead, routing key and data; in JSON mode { items }. With --retry or --drop, how many were settled; in JSON mode { ok, settled }.

List the next entries of a queue without consuming them. reads only queue-peek [-n <string>] [--limit=<string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> Queue node path. Option What it does -n <string> how many entries, from the front (default 10) --limit=<string> how many entries, from the front (default 10) queue-peek -n 20 /var/queues/pipeline-engine With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the next entries in delivery order: id, state (ready or in-flight), attempts, created, routing key and data; in JSON mode { items }.

Check stored reach against a walk of each path, for a sample of nodes and every account. reads only reach-check [--sample=<string>] Option What it does --sample=<string> how many nodes to judge (default 2000)

Create a bidirectional relation between two nodes. changes things relate [--reverse=<string>] <a> <b> <label> Argument What it is <a> first node. <b> second node. <label> relation label (both sides unless --reverse) Option What it does --reverse=<string> label for the b -> a side (default: same as label)
Remove reciprocal relation links when one side is deleted (long-running) administrators only · changes things relations-guard

The renditions made of every picture, video and recording, by role, from /etc/renditions.yaml. reads only renditions renditions JSON_OUTPUT=1 renditions With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each role: its section (image, video, audio, storyboard), its name, its file and its settings; in JSON the table by section and role.
Resolve node ID to path. reads only resolve-id <id> Argument What it is <id> id of node.
Reverse lines character-wise. reads only rev <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files to reverse, one after the other (stdin if omitted, or for -)

Remove (delete) files or directories. changes things rm [-r] [-f] [-d] <path> Argument What it is <path> node(s) to remove. Option What it does -r remove nodes and their contents recursively. -f ignore nonexistent nodes and arguments. -d remove empty directories (what rm without -r already does) rm /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg rm -r /archive/albums/Tomt_Exempelalbum With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing.

Remove empty directories. changes things rmdir [-p] <path> Argument What it is <path> empty directory node(s) to remove. Option What it does -p also remove each parent the path names, as each becomes empty. rmdir /home/exempel/tomt rmdir -p /home/exempel/utkast/2019/juni With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing.

Run a command line as another account, with only that account's rights and settings: for a service doing work on someone's behalf. administrators only · changes things runas <user> <line> Argument What it is <user> the account, by its username or uid. <line> the command line, as one argument or as its words. runas anna 'ls ~' runas anna touch /home/anna/note.txt

Copy files between EiN and another machine over SSH (members of group ssh) changes things scp [-r] [-p] [-q] [-B] [-P <number>] [-i <path>] [-F <path>] [-o <string>] <source>... <target> Argument What it is <source>... files to copy: EiN paths, or [user@]host:path. <target> where to: an EiN path, or [user@]host:path. Option What it does -r copy directories recursively. -p keep modes and modification times. -q no progress meter. -B batch mode: never ask for passwords or passphrases. -P <number> port (default 22) -i <path> identity file. -F <path> config file (default ~/.ssh/config; none: no file) -o <string> ssh option, e.g. StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new. scp anna@nas.local:photos/sailboat.jpg "/archive/albums/Summer 2020/" scp "anna@nas.local:photos/*.jpg" "/archive/albums/Summer 2020/" scp -r "/archive/albums/Summer 2020" anna@nas.local:backup/ With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; 1 when any file failed.

Faceted search over content: text, time, region, kind, tags, subjects (people, locations, devices) and containers. reads only search [-l <number>] [--limit=<number>] [--kind=<string>] [--tag=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--occasion=<string>] [--after=<string>] [--before=<string>] [--creator=<string>] [--subject=<string>] [--subject-name=<string>] [--under=<path>] [--include-stacked] [--within=<path>] [--undated] [--missing=<string>] [--has=<string>] [--like=<path>] [--bbox=<string>] [--circle=<string>] [--polygon=<string>] [--sort=<string>] [--at=<string>] [--facets] [--group-by=<string>] [--layout] [--cursor=<string>] [--above=<string>] [--max-scan=<number>] [--fields=<string>] [<query>] Argument What it is [<query>] search query text (optional). A year or date among the words (sailing 2011) is a time window, not words. A name that carries the window's one date, typed so or given as both --from and --to, is found though it has no date of its own: the album 'Autumn trip 2014' for 'autumn trip 2014'. Option What it does -l <number> page size (default 60, max 200) --limit=<number> page size (default 60, max 200) --kind=<string> content kind, comma-separated: photo, video, audio, document, or a node type (album, person, location, …) --tag=<string> filter by label (repeatable, intersected) --from=<string> taken at/after this date (2020, 2020-05, 2020-05-01) --to=<string> taken before this date, exclusive (--to 2000 includes all of 2000) --occasion=<string> taken on a holiday's days, every year of --from/--to (or every year): midsummer, midsommar, easter, påsk, christmas, jul, new-year, nyår, walpurgis, valborg, national-day, nationaldagen, lucia. --after=<string> alias for --from. --before=<string> alias for --to. --creator=<string> media created (uploaded or imported) by a user, by name or uid. --subject=<string> media a subject has, as : (person:anna-exempel, location:…, camera:…) or a path; any kind a subject- command answers for (repeatable, intersected). For a town or country use --bbox from location-region. --subject-name=<string> media of any subject of a kind whose name matches, as : (person:anna); repeatable groups intersect. --under=<path> media held by one album or directory (its own level; softlink members followed) --include-stacked with --under, include hidden stack members (internal aggregate mode) --within=<path> media anywhere in the tree under this directory, at any depth; by time, with the undated after the dated when there is no date window. Inside an unlisted tree (staging) it lists what the library's searches leave out. --undated only media with no capture time, in the order it arrived. --missing=<string> only what lacks this attr, dotted for a nested one (duplicate.deferred); repeatable, each must be missing. Quick on an attr core or a module keeps statistics on (labels, damage); on another one it may read the whole library. --has=<string> only what holds this value in an attr, as = : the attr is the value, or a list holding it (labels=sea); repeatable, each must hold. Quick on an attr core or a module indexes (labels, damage); on another one it may read the whole library. --like=<path> rank by how much each picture looks like this photo or video (more like this), or like a label's tag directory (/archive/tags/ , by its model), instead of by words; the other filters still narrow it. --bbox=<string> region as north,south,east,west. --circle=<string> region as lat,lng,radiusMeters. --polygon=<string> region as "lat,lng;lat,lng;lat,lng". --sort=<string> score | time | -time | name (default: score with a query, name for timeless kinds, -time otherwise) --at=<string> start the page at this date (2020, 2020-05, 2020-05-01); needs a time sort. --facets answer with per-year, per-month, per-kind and per-label counts instead of results. --group-by=<string> answer with the groups holding the matches, counted and dated, instead of results: the nearest ancestors of these node types (album), or the subjects of these kinds the matches have (person: who is in them, and how many of them show someone nobody has named) --layout answer with one compact complete layout index for a container or a subject (JSON only) --cursor=<string> resume token from a previous page (a position, for --subject/--under) --above=<string> the page ending just above this resume token — walking up a time-ordered browse. --max-scan=<number> candidates to examine before giving up (default 5000); store-counted and materialized facets are exact regardless. --fields=<string> extra fields to include: description, channels (a text hit's rank in each channel that found it), derivatives (with --layout: whether each file has renditions yet) search segelbåt --kind photo search --subject person:anna-exempel --subject person:bo-exempel --kind photo -- sort - time search --subject-name 'person:anna' --kind video search --bbox=$(location-region Exempelstad --bbox-only) --from 2007 --to 2007 search --occasion midsummer --from 1995 --to 2000 search --subject person:anna-exempel --group-by album search --under /archive/albums/Exempelalbum --group-by person search --like /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg --subject person:anna-exempel search --within /home/anna/staging/files -- sort time search --within /home/anna/staging/files --undated --facets search --within /home/anna/staging/files --missing duplicate.deferred search --has labels=sea --kind photo With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : a page of matching media, each with its path, name and date; with --group-by the albums (or other containers) holding the matches, or the people in them, instead, counted and dated; with --facets per-year, per-kind and per-label counts.

Stream editor for filtering and transforming text. reads only sed [-n] [-e <string>] [-E] [-r] <SCRIPT> <FILE>... Argument What it is <SCRIPT> sed script (e.g. s/foo/bar/g); omit when using -e. <FILE>... files to process (reads from stdin if omitted) Option What it does -n suppress automatic printing of pattern space. -e <string> add the script to the commands to be executed (repeatable) -E use extended regular expressions (patterns are JS regex) -r alias for -E.

Print a sequence of numbers. reads only seq [-s <string>] [-w] <LAST> <FIRST LAST> <FIRST INCREMENT LAST> Argument What it is <LAST> print numbers from 1 to LAST. <FIRST LAST> print numbers from FIRST to LAST. <FIRST INCREMENT LAST> print numbers from FIRST to LAST with INCREMENT. Option What it does -s <string> use STRING to separate numbers (default: newline) -w equalize width by padding with leading zeroes.
Manage system services. service <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

Add a service by linking to a service script directory. administrators only · changes things service-add <name> <path> Argument What it is <name> Service name. <path> Path to service script directory (must contain start.sh)
Disable a service. administrators only · changes things service-disable <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Enable a service. administrators only · changes things service-enable <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.

List services, with the module that ships each and how often it has restarted. reads only service-list [--detail] Option What it does --detail Also ask each running service for its own status line (its declared statusCommand)
Remove a service. administrators only · changes things service-remove <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Restart a service. administrators only · changes things service-restart <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Start a service. administrators only · changes things service-start <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Start all enabled services. administrators only · changes things service-start-all
Show service status. reads only service-status <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Stop a service. administrators only · changes things service-stop <name> Argument What it is <name> Service name.
Stop all running services. administrators only · changes things service-stop-all

Remove session and tty nodes left behind by dead shells. administrators only · changes things session-reap [--path=<string>] [--max=<string>] [--stale=<string>] [--dry-run] Option What it does --path=<string> Sessions directory (default $SESSIONS_PATH) --max=<string> Stop after removing this many nodes (default 1000) --stale=<string> Age at which an unstamped session is collectable (default 24h) --dry-run Report what would be removed without removing it.
Show and set who has access to a node. share <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.
Show who has access to a node, and through what. reads only share-info [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links.

Make, list, change and turn off links that open a node without signing in. visitors too · reads only share-link [--expires=<string>] [--never] [--as=<user>] [--session] <subcommand> <target> Argument What it is <subcommand> create | list | set | remove | open | reap. <target> create and list: the node; set and remove: the link id; open: the token. Option What it does --expires=<string> create and set: when the link stops working, a date or epoch ms (default: 30 days) --never create and set: the link does not expire. --as=<user> create: the link shows things as this account sees them, read-only, for a screen that never signs in (yours, or for an administrator one that is not an administrator's) --session open: act as the link in the whole session, not just this shell. share-link create /archive/albums/Exempelalbum share-link create /archive/dashboards/Kitchen.yaml --as display --never share-link list /archive/albums/Exempelalbum share-link remove 0123456789abcdef With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : create: the link and how many nodes it reached (ShareLinkCreated); list: ShareLink[]; set: ShareLink; open: what it opens (ShareLinkOpened).

Set who has access to nodes and everything below them. changes things share-set [--mode=<string>] [--owner=<string>] [--group=<string>] [--default-owner] [--reference=<path>] [-m <string>] [-x <string>] [-b] [--drop-links] [--pin] [--unpin] [--pinned-below] [--no-recursive] [--strict] [-L] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... paths to nodes. Option What it does --mode=<string> mode to set, octal or symbolic (e.g. 0750 or g+rx) --owner=<string> user to own the node, by name or uid (administrator only) --group=<string> group for the node, by name or gid (one the caller is in, unless administrator) --default-owner give the node the configured default owner and group (CFG_DEFAULT_SHARE_OWNER, CFG_DEFAULT_SHARE_GROUP) --reference=<path> share the node as this one is: its group, mode and acl (the owner stays) -m <string> add or modify an entry (u: : or g: : ) -x <string> remove an entry (u: or g: ) -b remove the user and group entries before applying -m (share links stay) --drop-links remove the share links' entries too, so no link opens the nodes. --pin hold this node against access changes made further up. --unpin let access changes from further up reach this node again. --pinned-below change the nodes below each path that hold their own access (--pin), not the path itself. --no-recursive change only this node, not what is below it. --strict exit non-zero when any node below could not be changed. -L do not follow symbolic links.
Delay for a specified amount of time. reads only sleep <seconds> Argument What it is <seconds> number of seconds to sleep.

Sort lines of text. reads only sort [-r] [-n] [-u] [-k <string>] [-t <string>] <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files whose lines are sorted together (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -r reverse the result of comparisons. -n compare according to string numerical value. -u output only unique lines. -k <string> sort by a key field (e.g., -k2) -t <string> use SEP as field separator.

Log in to another machine or run a command there (members of group ssh) changes things ssh [-p <number>] [-l <string>] [-i <path>] [-F <path>] [-o <string>] [-t] [-T] [-q] <destination> <command>... Argument What it is <destination> [user@]host, or a Host from ~/.ssh/config. <command>... command to run there instead of a shell. Option What it does -p <number> port (default 22) -l <string> remote user (default: your EiN user) -i <path> identity file (default: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, id_ecdsa, id_rsa) -F <path> config file (default ~/.ssh/config; none: no file) -o <string> HostName, Port, User, IdentityFile, StrictHostKeyChecking, BatchMode, ConnectTimeout, ServerAliveInterval, PasswordAuthentication; the same keywords are read from ~/.ssh/config. -t allocate a terminal for a command (-tt: even without one here) -T never allocate a terminal. -q quiet. ssh anna@nas.local ssh -p 2222 backup.example.com ssh nas.local 'df -h' ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new anna@nas.local uptime With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the remote exit status; 255 when the connection fails.

Install your public key in another machine's authorized_keys (members of group ssh) changes things ssh-copy-id [-i <path>] [-p <number>] [-o <string>] [-f] [-n] <destination> Argument What it is <destination> [user@]host. Option What it does -i <path> public key file (default: first of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub, id_ecdsa.pub, id_rsa.pub) -p <number> port (default 22) -o <string> ssh option, e.g. StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new. -f add the key even if it is already there. -n only show what would be added. ssh-copy-id anna@nas.local ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub -p 2222 anna@backup.example.com With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; JSON mode: { ok, added }.

Make an SSH key pair in ~/.ssh, show a fingerprint (-l) or forget a host key (-R) changes things ssh-keygen [-t <string>] [-b <number>] [-f <path>] [-C <string>] [-N <string>] [-q] [-l] [-y] [-R <string>] Option What it does -t <string> key type: ed25519 (default), ecdsa, rsa. -b <number> bits: RSA 3072 (default) or more, ECDSA 256/384/521. -f <path> key file (default ~/.ssh/id_ ) -C <string> comment (default @ein) -N <string> passphrase; asked for when omitted at a terminal. -q quiet. -l show the key file's fingerprint instead. -y print the public key of a private key file. -R <string> remove a host ([host]:port off port 22) from known_hosts. ssh-keygen ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C "backup key" ssh-keygen -l -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ssh-keygen -R nas.local With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; with -l the key size, fingerprint, comment and type.
Start an SSH server. administrators only · changes things ssh-server [--port=<string>] Option What it does --port=<string> port to use.

Bookmark nodes as softlinks in $HOME/stars (star ..., star -d ..., star [list]) reads only star [-d] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... nodes to star/unstar, or "list". Option What it does -d remove the star.

Display file or node status. reads only stat [-L] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to node. Option What it does -L do not follow symbolic links. stat /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the node's type, size, mode, owner and times.
Per-type archive growth: nodes and bytes added by year and month. reads only stats-overview
Which instance this is: host name, uptime, core's version and commit, the module API, each module's commit, and the PostgreSQL and Deno versions. reads only system-info

Output the last part of files, logs, or stdin (with -f to follow) reads only tail [-n <string>] [-c <string>] [-f] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] log/file/blob node to read (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -n <string> output the last NUM lines, or use +NUM for starting at line NUM (-NUM works too) -c <string> output the last NUM bytes, or use +NUM for starting at byte NUM. -f follow: keep the output live as the log/file grows.

Watch the system live: CPU graph, memory and event-loop lag, disks, pipeline work, running commands, sessions, services and recent problems. Keys: q quits, arrows scroll, s sorts, + and - change the interval, p pauses. reads only top [-d <number>] [-n <number>] Option What it does -d <number> Seconds between updates (default 2) -n <number> Write this many frames one after another and stop, as without a terminal. top top -d 5

Translate or delete characters. reads only tr [-d] [-s] [-c] <SET1> <SET2> Argument What it is <SET1> set of characters to translate from. <SET2> set of characters to translate to. Option What it does -d delete characters in SET1. -s squeeze repeated characters in last operand. -c use complement of SET1.

Move nodes into the reader's trash, alone or as one batch, list it, restore entries, or empty it. changes things trash [--batch=<string>] [--label=<string>] [--limit=<number>] [--older-than=<number>] [--all] <subcommand> <items>... Argument What it is <subcommand> put | list | restore | empty. <items>... put: paths to trash, at most 2000; restore and empty: entry ids, batch ids, or / for one entry of a batch. Option What it does --batch=<string> put: into one batch, the one with this id or, with no id, a new one (at most 2000 entries) --label=<string> put: what the batch is called in the trash. --limit=<number> restore: at most this many entries of each batch named. --older-than=<number> empty: only entries trashed more than this many days ago. --all empty: every user's trash (administrators) trash put /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg trash put --batch --label 'Copies of a sailboat' /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0002.jpg /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0003.jpg trash list trash restore 01J9Z8Q4R7XKD3V5B2N6M0PA1C -- limit 500 trash empty --older-than 30 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : put: the entries made and their batch (TrashPutResult); list: TrashEntry[], a batch as one row; restore: where each went, and what is left of the batches named (TrashRestoreResult); empty: how many were removed.

Truncate an associated resource of a node if it has one. changes things truncate [-s <string>] <path> Argument What it is <path> path to truncate. Option What it does -s <string> size to truncate to (default: 0)

Bundle modules' pages into /var/cache/ui for the Web UI to load, unless unchanged since the last build, and write the installation's third-party notices there. changes things ui-build [--all] <module>... Argument What it is <module>... Module to build; repeatable. Option What it does --all Every installed module with pages, and forget the bundles of those gone.
Tabler icons by name, as SVG markup, for the Web UI. reads only ui-icons <name>... Argument What it is <name>... Icon name: map-pin, heart-filled.
The Web UI's sidebar, top bar, panels and map layers for the caller, from every module's entries and the administrator's, the caller's groups' and the user's changes. reads only ui-nav

Report or omit repeated lines. reads only uniq [-c] [-d] [-u] [-i] [<INPUT>] Argument What it is [<INPUT>] file to read (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -c prefix lines by the number of occurrences. -d only print duplicate lines. -u only print unique lines. -i ignore differences in case when comparing.
Unmount a filesystem. administrators only · changes things unmount [--save] <path> Argument What it is <path> mount point. Option What it does --save also remove the mount from /etc/fstab.
Remove a bidirectional relation (both sides) changes things unrelate <a> <b> <label> Argument What it is <a> relation link path, or first node. <b> second node (with label) <label> relation label.

Expand a zip archive into a directory, streaming each entry. Refuses an archive with an entry that would land outside the directory, or whose files would not leave a tenth of their size free. A file already there at its entry’s size is left as it is, so a run that stopped can be run again. changes things unzip [-d <path>] [-n] [-o] [--as-upload] <archive> Argument What it is <archive> the zip to expand. Option What it does -d <path> the directory to expand into, made if missing (default: the current one) -n never write over an existing file (the default) -o write over an existing file. --as-upload take the files for the upload the archive came in: one of a type /etc/frozen-uploads lists is frozen, as an upload of it would be. unzip -d /home/anna/staging/files/inbox /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/takeout-001.zip unzip --as-upload -d /home/anna/staging/files/inbox /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/takeout-001.zip With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : in JSON mode, UnzipAnswer: the files, directories and bytes written, the files left as they were, and each entry not expanded with why. Exits non-zero when any entry was not expanded.
Manage users. user <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand to run.

Create a user account and its home with its own group (an existing group of its name when that group's gid is free as a uid) and link it into its own and its other groups. administrators only · changes things user-create [--uid=<string>] [--title=<string>] [--email=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--groups=<string>] <username> Argument What it is <username> name of the user to create: lower-case letters, digits and . _ -, starting with a letter or _. Option What it does --uid=<string> numeric user ID. --title=<string> display title for the user. --email=<string> e-mail address, which signs in like the username; no other account may have it. --description=<string> description of the user. --groups=<string> comma-separated groups to add it to besides its own; empty for none (default CFG_DEFAULT_USER_GROUPS)

Delete a user account, its home, its own group, and its open sessions; what it owned goes to another user. administrators only · changes things user-delete [--to=<user>] [--force] <username> Argument What it is <username> username to delete. Option What it does --to=<user> user that takes over the nodes it owned (default admin) --force force deletion even if errors occur.
Disable a user account and end its open sessions. administrators only · changes things user-disable <username> Argument What it is <username> username to disable.

Make this shell an administrator's, or with --session the whole sign-in, for a member of the sudo group, after entering the password again. changes things user-elevate [--password=<string>] [--session] [--off] Option What it does --password=<string> your own password (prompts if not given); --password= for one starting with a dash. --session the session's sign-in, every page and terminal of it, not just this shell's. --off make the shell, or with --session the sign-in, no longer an administrator's.
Enable a disabled user account. administrators only · changes things user-enable <username> Argument What it is <username> username to enable.
Check if a user account exists. reads only user-exists <username> Argument What it is <username> username to check.
List groups a user belongs to. reads only user-groups <user> Argument What it is <user> user to list groups for.
Print user and group IDs. reads only user-id [--uid=<string>] Option What it does --uid=<string> show identity for specified uid.
Display user account information. reads only user-info <username> Argument What it is <username> username to look up.

An account's sign-in link, with which its person chooses their own password at /invite/ : shown, made new (--new) or taken away (--off); for an administrator. reads only user-invite [--new] [--days=<string>] [--off] <username> Argument What it is <username> the account. Option What it does --new make a new link; one sent before stops working. --days=<string> with --new: how many days it works, 1 to 90 (default 7) --off take the link away. user-invite anna --new user-invite anna user-invite anna --off With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : UserInvite.

Which account a sign-in link is for, and with --password, choose its password with it, which spends the link and signs in. visitors too · reads only user-invite-accept [--password=<string>] [--session] <token> Argument What it is <token> the token after /invite/ in the link. Option What it does --password=<string> the account's new password; give it as --password= . --session sign in the whole session, not just this shell. user-invite-accept AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUv user-invite-accept AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUv --password=correct-horse --session With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : UserInviteAccepted.

List the user accounts; as JSON with each one's primary group, e-mail address, description, person and built-in role, and for an administrator whether a password is set. reads only user-list [--inactive] [--active] Option What it does --inactive show only inactive users. --active show only active users.

Change user password. changes things user-passwd [--username=<user>] [--old-password=<string>] [--new-password=<string>] <username> Argument What it is <username> username to change password for. Option What it does --username=<user> username (alternative to positional) --old-password=<string> current password: required but for an administrator, and checked whenever given. --new-password=<string> new password to set.
Resolve username to UID or vice versa. reads only user-resolve <uid_or_username> Argument What it is <uid_or_username> uid (numeric) or username to resolve.
Set a user's primary group. administrators only · changes things user-set-primary-group <user> <group> Argument What it is <user> user to change primary group for. <group> new primary group.

Update an account's display name, description and (an administrator only) e-mail address; anyone may update their own name and description. changes things user-update [--name=<string>] [--email=<string>] [--description=<string>] <username> Argument What it is <username> username to update. Option What it does --name=<string> set the display name, which cannot be empty. --email=<string> set the e-mail address, which signs in like the username; empty to remove it. --description=<string> set description.
Print the current username. visitors too · reads only user-whoami
Generate a random UUID. reads only uuid

Print newline, word, and byte counts of files or stdin. reads only wc [-c] [-m] [-l] [-w] <FILE>... Argument What it is <FILE>... files to count, each on a line of its own and then a total (stdin if omitted, or for -) Option What it does -c print the byte counts. -m print the character counts. -l print the newline counts. -w print the word counts. wc -l /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/notes.txt With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the counts asked for, then the file name; a total line when there are several files.

List who is signed in: each SSH login, terminal and Web UI connection, the address it connects from, its idle time and what it runs. Admin sees everyone's, anyone else their own. reads only who who With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One row per open session, oldest first.
Manage active Web UI. reads only www <command> [<name>] Argument What it is <command> Command: list, active, set, reset. [<name>] UI name to set as default.

Run a command with the items read from stdin as its arguments, as GNU xargs does: as many per run as fit, or -n per run, or one input line per run with -L, or once per line with -I replacing a string in the command. Items are separated by blanks and newlines, with quotes and backslashes as GNU has them; -0 and -d split on one character instead. The command reads an empty stdin, or the terminal with -o; with no command it is echo. -P runs several at once, -p asks before each run. Exits 123 when a run failed, 124 when one exited 255, 125 when one was killed, 126 or 127 when one could not run. reads only xargs [--null] [-0] [--delimiter=<string>] [-d <string>] [--max-args=<string>] [-n <string>] [--max-lines=<string>] [-L <string>] [--max-chars=<string>] [-s <string>] [--replace=<string>] [-I <string>] [--eof=<string>] [-E <string>] [--no-run-if-empty] [-r] [--verbose] [-t] [--interactive] [-p] [--open-tty] [-o] [--exit] [-x] [--max-procs=<string>] [-P <string>] [--arg-file=<path>] [-a <path>] [<command>...] Argument What it is [<command>...] the command to run and its first arguments; the items follow them (default: echo) Option What it does --null items end with a NUL character, as find -print0 writes them; quotes are not special. -0 items end with a NUL character, as find -print0 writes them; quotes are not special. --delimiter=<string> items end with this character, such as , or \n; quotes are not special. -d <string> items end with this character, such as , or \n; quotes are not special. --max-args=<string> at most this many items per run. -n <string> at most this many items per run. --max-lines=<string> at most this many input lines per run. -L <string> at most this many input lines per run. --max-chars=<string> at most this many characters per command line (default 131072) -s <string> at most this many characters per command line (default 131072) --replace=<string> run once per input line, with this string in the command replaced by the line, as -I {}. -I <string> run once per input line, with this string in the command replaced by the line, as -I {}. --eof=<string> an item equal to this ends the input. -E <string> an item equal to this ends the input. --no-run-if-empty run nothing when stdin is empty. -r run nothing when stdin is empty. --verbose write each command line to stderr before running it. -t write each command line to stderr before running it. --interactive ask on the terminal before each run, and run it only on an answer starting with y. -p ask on the terminal before each run, and run it only on an answer starting with y. --open-tty each command reads the terminal as its stdin, for an interactive one such as edit. -o each command reads the terminal as its stdin, for an interactive one such as edit. --exit with -n, stop when the items a run is given do not fit in -s, rather than giving it fewer; -L always does. -x with -n, stop when the items a run is given do not fit in -s, rather than giving it fewer; -L always does. --max-procs=<string> run up to this many commands at once (default 1); 0 runs as many as there are. -P <string> run up to this many commands at once (default 1); 0 runs as many as there are. --arg-file=<path> read the items from this file; the command then reads stdin. -a <path> read the items from this file; the command then reads stdin. find /home/anna/staging -name '*.tmp' -print0 | xargs -0 rm ls /archive/people | xargs -I {} info /archive/people/{} With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : what the commands it runs write; xargs itself writes text only.

Every setting of an EiN with all its modules: 107 of them, in the groups the Settings page shows. Configuration says where each value comes from and how to change it. Who it is for : everyone is a system setting, which only an administrator changes, on Settings → System or with config set ; each person is a preference everyone sets for themselves, on Profile → Preferences. Default : the value until someone changes it. A deployment can set another in .env , and a module can choose one. Restarts : the services a change restarts by itself. Work already running is picked up again when they are back.

Days the access log keeps sign-ins and downloads . How long the access log keeps its records: who signed in or out, opened a share link or downloaded what, and from where. 0 keeps them for good. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 365 Kind number Restarts access-log-purger

Album folders full check (seconds) . How often every album folder is compared with its album, beside following each change as it happens. This catches what a change notice missed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 3600 Kind number Restarts album-folders From the module Album folders

Album folders location . Where the albums are kept as folders of files, as the EiN server sees it. Empty means the folder albums beside the stored files. It must be on the same mount as the stored files, since each file there is a hard link to one of them. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty Kind string Restarts album-folders From the module Album folders

Stack similarity . How alike two neighbouring photos in an album must look to be stacked as one burst. Higher stacks only near-identical shots. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.75 Kind number Restarts album-metadata From the module Archive

Stack time gap (seconds) . How far apart in capture time two neighbouring photos may be and still be stacked together. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 10 Kind number Restarts album-metadata From the module Archive

Header entrance . How the tiles of a page's header arrive when the page opens: drawn as if by pen and filled from the bottom up, falling into place, sliding in from the right, swept in from left to right, growing from the bottom edge, rippling out from the title, snapping in like puzzle pieces, or a wave of light across them. A device set to reduce motion never animates it. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default drawn Choices drawn , falling , sliding , sweep , growing , ripple , puzzle , wave Kind select

Header entrance time . How many milliseconds the header's entrance takes, from the first tile starting to the last one in place. 0 shows the header as it is, without an entrance. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default 450 Kind number

Header over a cover . How the tiles of a page's header meet its cover photo: split gives the left of the header to the tiles, dissolving hat by hat into the photo along a slanted edge, with their outlines running on over it; lines lays only their outlines over the photo, fading out from the left. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default split Choices split , lines Kind select

Answer length (tokens) . How many tokens the model may write in one call when thinking is not asked for. A thinking model writes its thought inside the same budget, so it may need more. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 2048 Kind number From the module Assistant

Language model . The model name sent with each request. A llama.cpp server answers with whichever model it loaded, whatever this says. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default qwen3.5-4b Kind string Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Language model address . The base of an OpenAI-compatible chat API, without /v1: ours (a llama.cpp server) or a provider's, which is then named under Language model provider. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default http://127.0.0.1:8190 Kind string Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Language model key . The bearer key the provider expects, sent only to the language model address above. Unset when the server needs none. No shell sees it, and nothing shows it once it is set. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Language model provider . The provider's name when the language model is a service elsewhere (OpenAI, say). The chat names it and says that questions, and what the assistant reads in the archive to answer them, are sent there. Set by the host profile. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means ours, run on this host Kind string Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Think before answering . 1 asks the model to think before it answers in the chat, 0 asks it not to; llm-chat, and the search box through it, thinks only when given --think. Sent as llama.cpp's chat_template_kwargs, so only a server that reads them honours it. Empty sends nothing and the server decides. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the server decides Choices 1 , 0 Kind select From the module Assistant

Wait for the language model (seconds) . How long a question to the assistant waits for a language model that is not there, restarting or still loading its model, before the chat says the assistant is unavailable. The chat says it is waiting meanwhile. 0 gives up at once. The search box never waits; it reads the words without the model. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 180 Kind number From the module Assistant

Where our language model runs . card: on the graphics card, beside the share it leaves. cpu: on the processor. Set by the host profile; unused when a provider runs the model. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the host does not say Choices card , cpu Kind select Restarts llm-link From the module Assistant

Broker for devices . The broker's address as the devices on the network reach it, host:port, which a device added from the network is given. setup.sh --automation runs a listener beside the broker that says it. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the address the network listener says Kind string From the module Automation

Device MQTT password . The password of the device user, given only to a device added from the network. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell From the module Automation

Device MQTT user . The account a device added from the network signs in to the broker with. setup.sh --automation sets it to device. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means devices sign in without an account Kind string From the module Automation

Device sources . Which kinds of device the bridge listens for, and drives, separated by spaces: ha-discovery (anything that announces itself the way Home Assistant reads, such as ESPHome), shelly (Shelly's second generation and later) and shelly-gen1 (Shelly's first generation: Plug S, 1, 1PM, 2.5, i3). Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default ha-discovery shelly shelly-gen1 Kind string Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

Discovery prefix . The topic devices announce themselves under, for ha-discovery. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default homeassistant Kind string Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

MQTT broker . The broker devices talk to, as mqtt://host:1883 or mqtts://host:8883. setup.sh --automation runs one beside EiN, in the automation sidecar, and sets this. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means no device is heard on a broker; those EiN asks over the network are still read Kind string Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

MQTT password . The password of the MQTT user, sent only to the broker above. No shell sees it, and nothing shows it once it is set. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

MQTT user . The account EiN signs in to the broker with. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means EiN signs in without an account Kind string Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

Node docs in the editor . Whether the panel of a node in the automation editor shows, at its foot, what the node does and what each of its settings means. Folding or opening them there sets this. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default true Kind boolean From the module Automation

Reading history . How long an endpoint's values are kept. Applies to endpoints found from now on; one found before keeps its own (change it with attrs on the endpoint). Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 365 day Choices 30 day , 90 day , 365 day , forever Kind select Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

Restreamer . The restreamer cameras are given to and their streams read from, go2rtc's API as http://host:1984 . setup.sh --automation runs one beside EiN, in the automation sidecar, and sets this. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means a camera has no live view, and its picture is asked of the camera itself Kind string Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

Restreamer for the media service . The restreamer's RTSP as the media service reaches it, rtsp://host:8554, where it reads a camera's stream to watch it for faces. setup.sh --automation sets it. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means no other service is told where a camera's stream is, so none is watched for faces Kind string Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

Restreamer password . The password of the restreamer's account ein, sent only to the restreamer above. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

Seconds between readings . The shortest time between two numbers of one endpoint that are kept and published: a number that comes sooner waits, and only the newest of those is kept. On and off, words and presses are kept as they come. Given to endpoints found from now on, as their minInterval attr, which may be changed on each. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 10 Kind number Restarts automation-bridge From the module Automation

SNMP community . The read-only community EiN asks a device found on the network with when it adds it, and its snmp driver goes on asking it with: public unless the device was set to another. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default public Kind string From the module Automation

Confidence to start a new person from a face . How sure the detector must be of a face that matches nobody before it starts a new, unnamed person. Less certain faces stay unknown. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.7 Kind number From the module Archive

Face match threshold . How similar two faces must be before one is attached to a known person. Higher is stricter and produces fewer wrong matches but more unknown faces. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.56 Kind number From the module Archive

Face neighbour similarity . How similar a known face must be to count as a vote for its person. Faces less alike than this are ignored when deciding who an unknown face is. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.51 Kind number From the module Archive

Face neighbours compared . How many of the most similar known faces are compared with each unknown one. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 24 Kind number From the module Archive

Face winner margin . How far the leading person's votes must outweigh the runner-up's before a face is attached. 1.2 means 20% more; higher leaves close calls unknown. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 1.2 Kind number From the module Archive

Maximum head turn (degrees) . How far a head may be turned away from the camera, estimated from the eyes, nose and mouth, and still be kept as a face. Full profiles beyond this match the wrong person far more often. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 80 Kind number From the module Archive

Minimum face confidence . How sure the detector must be before a box is kept as a face that takes part in recognition. Below 0.7 most detections are backs of heads, blur or things that are not faces, and they pull strangers toward the wrong person. Applies to new detections; a box below it is not stored unless someone tags it by hand. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.7 Kind number From the module Archive

Minimum face size (px) . The shorter side a face box must have, in pixels of the displayed photo, to be kept as a face. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 24 Kind number From the module Archive

Size to start a new person from a face (px) . The shorter side, in pixels, a face that matches nobody must have before it starts a new, unnamed person. Small faces stay unknown rather than seeding people from blur. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 48 Kind number From the module Archive

Archive language . The language the archive is kept in: the order names are sorted in, the words it offers as labels, and how it describes how two people are related. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default en Choices en , sv Kind select

Date and time format . How dates and times are written in the browser, as a locale: sv-SE writes 2026-11-09 13:26 and 9 nov. 2026, en-SE 2026-11-09, 13:26 and 9 Nov 2026, en-GB 09/11/2026, 13:26, en-US 11/9/2026, 1:26 PM. Each person may choose their own. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default sv-SE Kind locale

Date and time format . How dates and times are written for you, as a locale: sv-SE writes 2026-11-09 13:26 and 9 nov. 2026, en-SE 2026-11-09, 13:26 and 9 Nov 2026, en-GB 09/11/2026, 13:26, en-US 11/9/2026, 1:26 PM. Empty follows the system setting. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default empty, which means the system's date and time format Kind locale

Media service address . Where EMS answers. Every model and media-tool request goes there; the models themselves are configured on the EMS side. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default http://127.0.0.1:8181 Kind string Restarts models , models-second , media-worker , ems-link , metrics-sampler , ems-files From the module Media service

Media service check interval (seconds) . How often the ems-link service asks whether EMS answers, and logs when that changes. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 60 Kind number Restarts ems-link From the module Media service

Media service file address . Where the media service reaches EiN's files, as host:port: the ems-files service's port as EMS sees it. Each request to EMS that names a file names it, and EMS reads that request's inputs and writes its outputs there, nothing else and only while the request runs. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means EMS reaches no files: every request that names one waits Kind string Restarts ems-files From the module Media service
Media service file port . The port the ems-files service listens on. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 2224 Kind number Restarts ems-files From the module Media service

Media service files over TLS . Encrypt the media service's file connections with TLS, each side pinning the other's certificate. Off, a connection proves it is the media service's with a secret and is not encrypted, which costs half the CPU and suits EMS on the same machine or network. Turn it on when EMS reaches EiN over a network you do not trust. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default false Kind boolean Restarts ems-files From the module Media service

Media service key . The bearer key EMS expects (the first word of a line in its keys file, which names this system as a caller), sent only to the media service address above. Unset when EMS runs without keys. No shell sees it, and nothing shows it once it is set. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell Restarts ems-link From the module Media service

Media service restart patience (seconds) . How long a batch request keeps retrying a refused connection before the step fails. EMS restarts refuse connections for tens of seconds; this is what keeps the steps in flight across one from failing for good. Interactive requests never wait. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 90 Kind number Restarts models , models-second , media-worker From the module Media service

Media service's share of the graphics card (MB) . The most of the graphics card the media service's models hold, in MB; a model that needs more than is left runs on the processor instead, slower. 0 keeps every model on the processor. Leave room for a language model on the same card by lowering it. The media service's page sets it with the slider under the card. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the media service's own share (EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB), by default the whole card Kind number Restarts ems-link From the module Media service

Module sources . Where published modules are looked for: organisations on GitHub, Forgejo or Gitea, as their addresses separated by spaces, such as https://github.com/einhq . Each repository named module- in them is a module. A module installed by name comes from the first source that has it, and a module's dependencies from its own organisation first. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default https://github.com/einhq Kind string

Tokens for module sources . Access tokens for module sources that are not public, as host=token separated by spaces, such as forge.example:3000=… github.com=…. Each token is sent to its own host only. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default none: a key is set by you, and never shown again Kind a key: never readable, in no shell

Look up the weather . Let EiN ask SMHI and Open-Meteo what the weather was at a place and time, for photos and for the days of a track's trips, and Open-Meteo for the forecast a dashboard's weather card shows. Each lookup sends the coordinates and the date to them; turn it off to keep them from being sent. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default true Kind boolean From the module Archive

SMHI station distance (km) . How far from a place the nearest SMHI weather station may be and still give its weather. Farther away, and outside Sweden, the weather comes from Open-Meteo's reanalysis instead. 0 leaves SMHI out. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 30 Kind number From the module Archive
Ken Burns effect . Slowly pan and zoom each photo during a slideshow. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default true Kind boolean From the module Archive
Seconds per slide . How long each photo is shown in a slideshow. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default 3 Kind number From the module Archive

Entry pipeline reservation (%) . Share of trigger claims that first try pipelines declaring options.entryPoint. Empty reserved claims fall back to the ordinary fair rotation. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0 Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine

Gap check interval (seconds) . How often the background check looks for media missing something a pipeline should have given it, when nothing else is waiting to be processed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 900 Kind number Restarts media-heal From the module Archive

Keep transcripts current . Videos and recordings transcribed with other speech-recognition settings than the media service runs now are transcribed again in the background, behind new media. Set to "off" to leave existing transcripts alone. On a large library a change of settings means hours of background work. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty Kind string From the module Media

Media worker budget . How much media work the media-worker service runs at once: thumbnails, renditions, fingerprints, face matching, duplicates and staging. Each job declares what it costs, so one video transcode can exclude a face assignment on a small box. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 2 Kind number Restarts media-worker From the module Media

Media worker jobs in flight . Upper bound on the media worker's concurrent jobs. The budget above is the real limit; this only caps how many can be in flight. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 4 Kind number Restarts media-worker From the module Media

Media worker slots for downstream work . Soft reservation in the media worker's budget for work after ingest. Ingest borrows unused slots, but ready downstream jobs get them first so a continuous ingest backlog cannot starve the rest of the pipeline. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 1 Kind number Restarts media-worker From the module Media

Model backlog rotation (ms) . How long the models worker stays on one backlog (faces, picture vectors, text in pictures, text vectors, transcripts, voices) before rotating to the next when work remains on more than one. Faces outrank the other backlogs and a crawl finds new ones continuously, so without this they would starve the rest outright. Each rotation costs the media service a minute or two of loading models and of slots waiting for the last long step of the old backlog, so an hour puts throughput before the wait of the other backlogs; a backlog with no work hands its turn on at once either way. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 3600000 Kind number Restarts models From the module Media

Model requests in flight . How many model-bound media steps (faces, picture vectors, text in pictures, text vectors, transcripts, voices) EiN keeps in flight against the media service at once. Whether each runs on the GPU or the CPU is the media service's decision; size this against its own model limit, since more slots than it runs at once only move the wait into its queue. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 2 Kind number Restarts models From the module Media
Pipeline cleanup interval (seconds) . How often finished pipeline instances are pruned. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 3600 Kind number Restarts pipeline-pruner

Pipeline instances held open . How many pipeline instances the engine holds open at once, including those waiting on a worker pool. Every stuck sweep re-advances each open instance, so raise it together with the sweep interval. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 5000 Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine

Pipeline steps in parallel . How many inline pipeline steps the engine runs at once. Steps that are GPU- or CPU-heavy go to a worker pool instead and are bounded separately. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 4 Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine
Queue consume concurrency . How many queue entries the engine consumes in parallel. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 4 Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine

Quiet step warning (ms) . How long a running pipeline step may go without writing any output before the pipeline overview flags it. A flagged step keeps running: no step is ever stopped for taking long. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 1800000 Kind number

Rest after a full gap check (seconds) . How long the background gap check waits after a pass through the whole archive that found nothing before it starts another. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 21600 Kind number Restarts media-heal From the module Archive

Second models worker's slots . Slots of a second worker for the model-bound media steps, which goes through the same backlogs in the reverse order, so the media service runs a second model family beside the first worker's. 0 leaves it off. Size both workers' slots together against the media service's model limit, and mind its card: two families' models must fit there, or one runs on the CPU. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0 Kind number Restarts models-second From the module Media

Steps held in flight . How many dispatched steps the engine holds in memory before it stops claiming triggers. Work beyond it waits in the pool, where it costs nothing. Empty means 25 times the pipeline steps in parallel. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means 25 × pipeline steps in parallel Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine

Stuck sweep interval (ms) . How often, at most, the engine re-advances its open instances to repair any that stopped without finishing, and how long it backs off while admission is full. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 60000 Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine

Trigger concurrency . How many pipeline triggers the engine evaluates at once against incoming VFS events. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 4 Kind number Restarts pipeline-engine

Worker backlog rotation (ms) . How long a pipeline worker that serves several kinds of job stays on one before rotating to the next when work remains on both. 0 always takes the highest-priority kind. Applies to workers whose service does not set its own rotation. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0 Kind number Takes effect Read by each pipeline worker when it starts: restart the services that run one.

Command finder . The command that finds shell commands by what they are for, in the documentation's command search. Empty matches the words against command names and descriptions. The assistant sets itself here when it is installed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means a match on names and descriptions Kind string

Language model command . The command that asks a language model, for reading what a person writes as they write it — the search box's parser reads people, locations and words with it. Empty asks no model. The assistant sets itself here when it is installed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means no model Kind string

Search parser . The command that reads what is typed into the search box as filters — people, locations, years, kinds. Empty searches the words as they are. Archive sets its parser here when it is installed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the words as they are Kind string

Text embedder . The command that turns texts into vectors, for finding by meaning — the command finder ranks commands with it. Empty finds by words alone. The media service sets itself here when it is installed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means by words alone Kind string

Session cleanup interval (seconds) . How often expired sessions and stranded terminals are collected, and expired share links turned off. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 3600 Kind number Restarts session-reaper

Session cookie lifetime . How long a browser keeps its session cookie. Refreshed on every navigation, so this bounds idleness rather than total session age. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 86400 Kind number

Session expiry . How long after its last activity a session is collected by the reaper. A session keeps the value it was created with; one holding an open terminal is never collected, whatever this says. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 43200 Kind number

Share link session expiry . How long a browser that opened a share link keeps it while unused: its cookie, and its session after its last activity. Never past the link's own end. A screen showing a dashboard is rarely reloaded, so this is longer than a sign-in's. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 2592000 Kind number

Terminal reconnect grace . How long an interactive terminal survives without a browser connection, allowing reloads and short network interruptions to reattach. A change applies from the next disconnect. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 300 Kind number

How widely what you create is shared . Where anything you create as shared starts out: private, shared with its group, or with everyone who has an account. "Default" follows the system setting. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default default Choices default , private , shared , everyone Kind select
Shell history length . How many commands the terminal remembers between sessions. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default 1000 Kind number

Hours in /tmp . How long a file left in /tmp, such as a picture sent to search with, is kept before it is removed. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 24 Kind number Restarts tmp-sweeper

Todo widget . A button floating over every page, which you can drag anywhere: it counts the todos about what is on screen — the picture in the lightbox, an album, a person — and lists them, or adds one about it. Who it is for Each person (Profile → Preferences) Default false Kind boolean From the module Todo

Silence that splits speech (ms) . How long a pause must be before transcription treats it as the end of a stretch of speech. Empty uses the media service's own setting. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the media service decides Kind number From the module Media service

Transcription language . The language spoken in recordings, as a code such as sv or en, sent with every transcription. Empty lets the media service detect it, or use its own default. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the media service decides Kind string From the module Media service

Word timings . 1 asks transcription for the time of every word, 0 for timings per segment only. Empty uses the media service's own setting. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the media service decides Choices 1 , 0 Kind select From the module Media service
Days in the trash . How long a trashed file stays restorable before it is removed for good. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 30 Kind number Restarts trash-purger

Default group . The group anything created as shared belongs to. This is the grant that lets the rest of the household see it. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default users Kind group

Default groups for new users . The groups a new account joins besides its own, as a comma-separated list of names. The New user form starts with them ticked, and user-create takes them unless --groups names others. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default users Kind string

Default owner . Who owns anything created as shared; a private album stays its creator's. Leave empty to let whoever creates it own it. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default empty, which means the person who creates it Kind user

Default permissions . Who may see and who may change anything created as shared: its owner, its group and everyone else, each with no access, view or edit. Everyone else is visitors who are not signed in, where they may browse, and anyone with an account outside the group. Kept as an octal mode, as in 0750. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0750 Kind mode

Visitors may browse . Whether someone who has not signed in may browse the archive as the guest, seeing what is shared with visitors, rather than being asked to sign in. Off, the guest can only sign in or open a share link, in the Web UI and through the API alike. Only on does the assistant's language model answer them. Off for a family's own archive; on for a public demo. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default false Kind boolean

Lip-sync vote weight . How much it counts, as a similarity, that a person's face is seen speaking in step with the voice. Only voices someone named or locked are weighed against it. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.9 Kind number From the module Archive

Minimum lip-sync score . How clearly a face must be seen speaking in step with a voice before that counts as a vote at all. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.6 Kind number From the module Archive

Speech to start a new person (seconds) . How long a voice that matches nobody must have spoken in a recording, in all, before it starts a new, unnamed person. Voices heard for less stay unknown. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 10 Kind number From the module Archive

Voice likeness to the person . How similar a voice must be to the average of a person's voices before it joins them. Stops a person drifting from one speaker to the next through a chain of loosely similar voices. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.7 Kind number From the module Archive

Voice likeness to the person seen speaking . How similar a voice must be to the average of a person's voices before a face seen speaking with it may join them. Lower than the plain likeness bar, since the face is evidence too; it stops the camera operator's voice going to whoever is in frame. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.5 Kind number From the module Archive

Voice match threshold . How similar a voice in a recording must be to a known voice before it is attached to that person. Higher is stricter and produces fewer wrong matches but more unknown speakers. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.55 Kind number From the module Archive

Voice neighbour similarity . How similar a known voice must be to count as a vote for its person. Voices less alike than this are ignored when deciding who is speaking. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 0.5 Kind number From the module Archive

Voice neighbours compared . How many of the most similar known voices are compared with each unknown one. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 24 Kind number From the module Archive

Voice winner margin . How far the leading person's votes must outweigh the runner-up's before a voice is attached. 1.2 means 20% more; higher leaves close calls unknown. Who it is for Everyone (an administrator sets it) Default 1.2 Kind number From the module Archive
The variables EiN reads or sets, apart from its settings ( CFG_… ), which are on Settings . In the shell, docs env lists them with their values there.

Read once, from EiN's own environment, when it starts: .env in an installation made with the installer. No shell has them, and none is shown back, since POSTGRES_URL carries the database's password. Variable Default What it is POSTGRES_URL postgres://ein:ein@127.0.0.1:5432/ein The PostgreSQL database holding the whole tree. POSTGRES_POOL_MAX 20 Database connections the process may hold at once. Parallel work queues on this long before PostgreSQL itself is the limit.
