Manage albums (create, info, list, set, add or move files) reads only album [--name=<string>] [--share=<string>] [--create] [--description=<string>] [--cover=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--cursor=<string>] <subcommand> <path> <files>... Argument What it is <subcommand> create | info | list | set | add | move. <path> album path. <files>... add: the files to put in the album: linked, or moved there out of staging; move: the files or links to move into the album; info: more albums, up to 50 in all. Option What it does --name=<string> create, add or move --create: the album display name (defaults to the slug) --share=<string> create, add or move --create: who sees it (default, private, shared, everyone; default: as your new albums are) --create add, move: make the album first when it is not there. --description=<string> album description (create) --cover=<string> cover media path (create) --limit=<string> albums per list page (max 1000) --cursor=<string> list: the last name of the page before (pages are in the store's name order) album info /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album info /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 /archive/albums/Sommar_2020 album create /archive/albums/Nytt_Exempelalbum --name 'Nytt exempelalbum' album set /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 spanStart 2019-05-30 album set /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 next /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2020 album create /archive/albums/Stugan --name 'Stugan' --share private album add /archive/albums/Sommar_2020 /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0001.jpg --create --name 'Sommar 2020' album move /archive/albums/Sommar_2020 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/IMG_0412.jpg /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/IMG_0413.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : for info , each album's list row with its id, cover, neighbours in a series and child count, a suggested album's parts and candidate albums, and the paths that name none (AlbumInfoAnswer); for list , the albums under a root, a suggested album's with what staging decides it by and its best match (AlbumListResult); for add , the files linked and moved and where each now files, whether it made the album, and the staging journal entries that undo the moves (AlbumAddResult); for move , each file moved and where it now is, the links removed, and what was already there or did not move (AlbumMoveResult); for create and set , nothing.

Give an album without a cover a random one of its own pictures (coverPhoto softlink) changes things album-cover [--all] [--stale] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] <album> Argument What it is <album> album path (repeatable) Option What it does --all every album in the tree but the staging suggestions. --stale only albums that have no cover yet (the default; accepted for symmetry with album-span) --limit=<number> stop after this many albums. --verbose print each album as it is written. album-cover /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album-cover --all --stale -- limit 50 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a coverPhoto softlink is written for each album that had none.

Put devices on an album's list, whose tracks its map draws. changes things album-device-add <album> <device>... Argument What it is <album> the album. <device>... devices: a name, a path under /dev, or a track of one. album-device-add /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 sailboat album-device-add /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 /dev/sailboat

The devices whose tracks an album's map draws: those the cameras of its media are linked to and those added by hand, and the devices of its media taken off the list. reads only album-device-list <album> Argument What it is <album> the album, or a folder in one. album-device-list /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 JSON_OUTPUT=1 album-device-list /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each listed device's path, name and tracks, whether cameras of the album's media are linked to it (and how many of the media they took) or it was added by hand; and the devices of its media taken off the list.

Take devices off an album's list, whose tracks its map draws. changes things album-device-rm <album> <device>... Argument What it is <album> the album. <device>... devices: a name, a path under /dev, or a track of one. album-device-rm /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 sailboat album-device-rm /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 /dev/sailboat

Build the profile staging matches suggested groups against, beside each library album as its .profile: its members' times, days, places and people, and the pictures that stand for it. changes things album-profile [--all] [--stale] [--force] <album>... Argument What it is <album>... library albums to profile; anything else is passed over. Option What it does --all every library album, a page at a time. --stale with --all: only albums with no profile, or one not checked for a week. --force build again even when the members are as they were. album-profile /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album-profile --all album-profile --all --stale With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many albums were looked at, how many profiles were written, already current and passed over, how long it took, and the albums that failed (AlbumProfileResult).
The path of one album somebody made, at random. reads only album-random

Write an album's time span (timeStart/timeEnd/mediaCount) onto the album node: its media's, widened to the days set by hand (spanStart/spanEnd) and to its trip. changes things album-span [--all] [--stale] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] [--dry-run] <album> Argument What it is <album> album path (repeatable) Option What it does --all every album in the tree but the staging suggestions. --stale only albums that have no span yet. --limit=<number> stop after this many albums. --verbose print each album as it is written. --dry-run answer each album's span and its media's without writing. album-span /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 album-span --all --stale album-span --dry-run /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many albums were scanned and updated, and each written album (each scanned one with --dry-run): its span, media count, first and last capture, and the hand-set ends still in force.

Reconcile album-local stacks of consecutive, perceptually similar photos. changes things album-stack [--all] [--dry-run] [--threshold=<number>] [--max-gap-seconds=<number>] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] <action> <album> <file> Argument What it is <action> refresh, front, separate, allow, stack or unstack. <album> album path. <file> member path for front/separate/allow/unstack; two or more for stack. Option What it does --all refresh every album but the staging suggestions. --dry-run report without writing manifests or links. --threshold=<number> minimum cosine of adjacent photos' SSCD fingerprints (default 0.75) --max-gap-seconds=<number> maximum adjacent capture-time gap (default 10) --limit=<number> stop after this many albums. --verbose print one line per album. album-stack refresh /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 --dry-run -v album-stack front /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : refresh: how many albums were scanned and changed, stacks and stacked photos, and per album its manifest; the others: the album and member acted on.

Birthdays, memorials and wedding anniversaries around a day, nearest first, with the age or years married. reads only anniversaries [--today=<string>] [--days-ahead=<string>] [--days-past=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--kind=<string>] [--people=<path>] Option What it does --today=<string> the day to look around, YYYY-MM-DD (default today, UTC) --days-ahead=<string> days after it to look at (default 30) --days-past=<string> days before it to look at (default 0) --limit=<string> at most this many (default 12) --kind=<string> only these, separated by commas: birthday, death, anniversary (death is a memorial, anniversary a wedding's) --people=<path> the folder of people to look in (default the archive's people) anniversaries anniversaries --kind birthday --days-ahead 60 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : One entry per occurrence, nearest first: kind, date, daysAway, years, milestone, title, path, and people, whose faces it shows.

Derive the archive's domain events, of its media analysis, staging, albums and locations, from VFS mutations (long-running) changes things archive-bridge archive-bridge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; it runs until stopped, turning VFS mutations into the archive's events.

Turn a written search into search filters (kinds, years, people and locations as subjects, an area, what the pictures show) reads only archive-parse [--rules] <query> Argument What it is <query> the search as written, a sentence or a few words. Option What it does --rules only the deterministic pass: years and kinds, no model and no name lookups. archive-parse 'Anna Andersson Göteborg 2019' archive-parse --rules 'filmer från 2010' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : text, kinds, from, to, people (with slug when one person), locations (a location node or an area), region, unresolved, source (llm or rules) and a one-line explain.

Match an image's detected faces to existing people, creating unnamed people for the rest. changes things assign-faces [--vote-threshold=<string>] [--attach-threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-create-confidence=<string>] [--min-create-size=<string>] [--no-create] [--reassign] [--allow-duplicate-person] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to the image file. Option What it does --vote-threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.51) --attach-threshold=<string> min winning vote weight to attach to a person (default 0.56) --margin=<string> winner must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) -k <string> neighbours to consider per face (default 24) --min-create-confidence=<string> min detection confidence to seed a new person (default 0.7) --min-create-size=<string> min face box side in px to seed a new person (default 48) --no-create attach only; never create an unnamed person. --reassign also re-decide faces a previous automatic run assigned. --allow-duplicate-person permit one person on two faces of the same image. --dry-run report without writing. --verbose print each face. assign-faces /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg assign-faces --dry-run --no-create /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each detected face with the person it was matched to, the score, and whether a new unnamed person was created.

Match a recording's voices to existing people, creating unnamed people for the rest. changes things assign-speakers [--vote-threshold=<string>] [--attach-threshold=<string>] [--person-threshold=<string>] [--asd-person-threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-create-seconds=<string>] [--asd-vote-weight=<string>] [--asd-min-score=<string>] [--no-create] [--reassign] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to the audio or video file. Option What it does --vote-threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.5) --attach-threshold=<string> min winning vote weight to attach to a person (default 0.55) --person-threshold=<string> min cosine similarity to the mean of the winner's voices (default 0.7) --asd-person-threshold=<string> the same, for the person a confident lip-sync match names (default 0.5) --margin=<string> winner must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) -k <string> neighbours to consider per voice (default 24) --min-create-seconds=<string> min seconds a voice spoke in all to seed a new person (default 10) --asd-vote-weight=<string> weight of a lip-sync match, as a similarity (default 0.9) --asd-min-score=<string> ignore a lip-sync match weaker than this (default 0.6) --no-create attach only; never create an unnamed person. --reassign also re-decide voices a previous automatic run assigned. --dry-run report without writing. --verbose print each voice. assign-speakers /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV assign-speakers --dry-run /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each voice with the person it was matched to and the score.

Weigh media against the library albums they may belong in, as staging weighs its suggested groups, and write nothing. reads only auto-album-assign [--per=<string>] [--root=<path>] [--top=<string>] [--holdout] [--evidence] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... files, albums, suggested groups or directories to match. Option What it does --per=<string> what one subject is: each path (group, the default), each media file (file), or all of it (set) --root=<path> only albums under this directory (default /archive/albums) --top=<string> candidates per subject (default 3) --holdout weigh the albums holding the subjects' media as if those media were not in them. --evidence each candidate's evidence, beside its reasons. auto-album-assign /home/anna/staging/albums/inbox/2019-06-14 --evidence auto-album-assign /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0001.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0002.jpg --per set --top 5 auto-album-assign /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg --per file --holdout With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each subject's media, how many are dated, its candidate albums best first with how likely and why, how likely a new album is, the margin and how sure (AlbumMatchReport).

Show how the staging organizer would group the media at and under some paths (directories, albums or files) into suggested albums, writing nothing. reads only auto-album-cluster [--user=<string>] [--strategy=<string>] [--significance=<string>] [--home=<string>] [--members] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... directories (everything within), albums (their members) or files. Option What it does --user=<string> whose home and household count (default the staging area's owner, else you) --strategy=<string> how to group (events, folders, none; default the category's, else events) --significance=<string> how readily a day is a group of its own (fewer, normal, more; default the category's, else normal) --home=<string> home for every year, as lat,lng or a location path (default the residence each year, else the densest cell) --members list each group's member paths. auto-album-cluster /home/anna/staging/files/inbox auto-album-cluster /archive/albums/2019-lake --members --significance more With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutoAlbumClusterReport: the media read, the home each year, and the groups proposed, by kind.

Camera and recording camera management. camera <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand: create, info, update, list, match, scan, link, relink, set-owner, remove-owner, cover, timeline, device.

Record a clip of a camera's stream now, filed under the camera like a clip around a face. changes things camera-clip [--post=<string>] <device> Argument What it is <device> the camera, by its device name or path. Option What it does --post=<string> seconds from now the clip lasts, 1 to 60 (10) camera-clip front-door camera-clip /dev/front-door --post 30

Give a camera without a cover of its own its newest picture, or its newest video with thumbnails (coverPhoto softlink) changes things camera-cover [--all] [--media] [--verbose] <camera> Argument What it is <camera> camera path, or with --media a media file (repeatable) Option What it does --all every camera. --media the paths are media files: cover the camera each is linked to. --verbose print each camera as its cover is written. camera-cover /archive/cameras/Canon_EOS_5D camera-cover --all camera-cover --media /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/clip.mp4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a coverPhoto softlink to its newest picture (or video) is written for each camera without a cover somebody chose.

Create a camera node and link the media already carrying its fingerprint. changes things camera-create [--name=<string>] [--make=<string>] [--model=<string>] [--serial=<string>] [--timezone=<string>] [--digitizer] [--quicktime-utc] [--description=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the camera node (default: /archive/cameras/ ) Option What it does --name=<string> display name (required) --make=<string> manufacturer, as exif writes it. --model=<string> model, as exif writes it. --serial=<string> serial number (the strong match key) --timezone=<string> IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Stockholm. --digitizer scanner whose camera dates are digitisation times, not capture times. --quicktime-utc keeps its videos' QuickTime CreateDate in UTC (phones), not local time. --description=<string> free-text note.

Link a camera to the device it is part of, such as a phone's camera to the phone whose track says where it was, or take the link away. changes things camera-device [--off] <camera> <device> Argument What it is <camera> the camera, by its path or its slug. <device> the device, by its name, its path, or a track of it. Option What it does --off take the link away. camera-device anna-phone anna-phone camera-device /archive/cameras/anna-phone /dev/anna-phone camera-device anna-phone --off

Have the media service watch every camera for faces, and file what it sees: the person on the camera's faces log, the face's picture and a clip around it under the camera (the camera-faces service) administrators only · changes things camera-faces service restart camera-faces
Show camera details and owners. reads only camera-info <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to camera node.

Link a file to its capture camera using extracted exif, or to a camera named by hand. changes things camera-link [--camera=<path>] [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to media file; with --camera, files or directories (repeatable) Option What it does --camera=<path> link to this camera instead of matching the exif (directories link the files directly in them) -v Verbose output.
List all cameras. reads only camera-list <root> Argument What it is <root> Camera directory (default: /archive/cameras)

Match a camera by serial number or make/model. reads only camera-match [--serial=<string>] [--make=<string>] [--model=<string>] [--root=<string>] Option What it does --serial=<string> Camera serial number. --make=<string> Camera manufacturer. --model=<string> Camera model. --root=<string> Camera directory (default: /archive/cameras)

Link existing media to a registered camera by its fingerprint. changes things camera-relink [--all] [--force] [--dry-run] [--reapply] <camera> Argument What it is <camera> VFS path to camera node (omit with --all) Option What it does --all sweep every registered camera that has a fingerprint. --force relink files already claimed by another camera. --dry-run report what would change without writing. --reapply link nothing; only re-date the files already linked (after a clock setting changed)

Unlink a person from a camera (removes both halves) changes things camera-remove-owner <camera> <person> Argument What it is <camera> VFS path to camera node. <person> VFS path to person node, or the owner link name.
Propose cameras seen in media but not registered. reads only camera-scan [--limit=<string>] Option What it does --limit=<string> max proposals to report (default 100)

Link a person as owner of a camera (dated relation pair) changes things camera-set-owner [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--update] <camera> <person> Argument What it is <camera> VFS path to camera node. <person> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --from=<string> ownership start date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --to=<string> ownership end date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --update rewrite the dates of an existing owner; an omitted date is cleared.

One camera's history as a chronological feed: owners getting and giving it up, its events and the albums with photos it took. reads only camera-timeline [--no-albums] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to camera node. Option What it does --no-albums skip the albums, which are most of the cost. camera-timeline /archive/cameras/canon-eos With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the camera's history in order: owners getting and giving it up, its events and the albums with photos it took.

Change a camera's settings. changes things camera-update [--name=<string>] [--make=<string>] [--model=<string>] [--serial=<string>] [--timezone=<string>] [--clock-offset=<string>] [--clock-from=<string>] [--digitizer] [--quicktime-utc] [--description=<string>] [--clips=<string>] [--clip-days=<string>] [--clear=<string>] <camera> Argument What it is <camera> VFS path to camera node. Option What it does --name=<string> display name. --make=<string> manufacturer, as exif writes it. --model=<string> model, as exif writes it. --serial=<string> serial number (the strong match key) --timezone=<string> IANA timezone its clock was set to, e.g. Europe/Stockholm. --clock-offset=<string> how far its clock ran ahead of the time in its zone, e.g. +23h2m, -5m, 0 once right. --clock-from=<string> with --clock-offset: the date it applies from (all its pictures without it) --digitizer mark as a scanner and suppress its camera dates on linked media. --quicktime-utc read its videos' QuickTime CreateDate as UTC (phones), not local time. --description=<string> free-text note. --clips=<string> what opens a clip of its device's stream: face (the default), motion (a face or motion) or off. --clip-days=<string> days its clips are kept (30); 0 keeps them. --clear=<string> remove a field (repeatable)

Recognize untagged faces as existing people (label propagation) + optionally create unnamed people for leftover clusters. changes things cluster-faces [--threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [--min-votes=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-cluster=<string>] [--cluster-threshold=<string>] [--max-cluster=<string>] [--max-people=<string>] [--create-people] [--mutual] [--no-mutual] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.51) --margin=<string> winning person must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) --min-votes=<string> min winning vote weight to assign (default 0.51) -k <string> nearest neighbours per face (default 8) --min-cluster=<string> min faces in a new-person cluster (default 3) --cluster-threshold=<string> stricter min similarity to group two untagged faces (default 0.61) --max-cluster=<string> skip clusters larger than this as likely chained (default 60) --max-people=<string> max unnamed people to create per run (default 500) --create-people create an unnamed person per leftover cluster (off by default) --mutual keep only mutual nearest-neighbour edges (on with --create-people) --no-mutual disable the mutual-neighbour filter. --dry-run report recognitions without writing personId. --verbose print each recognition. cluster-faces --create-people --min-cluster 4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many faces were recognised as existing people and how many clusters became new unnamed people.

Recognize untagged speech turns as existing people (label propagation) + optionally create unnamed people for leftover clusters. changes things cluster-voices [--threshold=<string>] [--margin=<string>] [--min-votes=<string>] [-k <string>] [--min-cluster=<string>] [--cluster-threshold=<string>] [--max-cluster=<string>] [--max-people=<string>] [--create-people] [--mutual] [--no-mutual] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --threshold=<string> min cosine similarity for a neighbour vote (default 0.5) --margin=<string> winning person must beat runner-up by this factor (default 1.2) --min-votes=<string> min winning vote weight to assign (default 0.5) -k <string> nearest neighbours per turn (default 8) --min-cluster=<string> min turns in a new-speaker cluster (default 3) --cluster-threshold=<string> stricter min similarity to group two untagged turns (default 0.6) --max-cluster=<string> skip clusters larger than this as likely chained (default 60) --max-people=<string> max unnamed people to create per run (default 500) --create-people create an unnamed person per leftover cluster (off by default) --mutual keep only mutual nearest-neighbour edges (on with --create-people) --no-mutual disable the mutual-neighbour filter. --dry-run report recognitions without writing personId. --verbose print each recognition. cluster-voices --create-people --min-cluster 4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many speech turns were recognised and how many clusters became new unnamed people.

List media taken on a given day (MM-DD, default today) in past years. reads only dayinhistory [--years=<number>] [--per-year=<number>] [<day>] Argument What it is [<day>] day as MM-DD (default today) Option What it does --years=<number> years with media to collect, newest first (default 8) --per-year=<number> media kept per year, earliest first (default 4) dayinhistory dayinhistory 06-21 --years 20 --per-year 1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : monthDay, and the years that have media taken on that day, newest first, each with its first media.

Detect faces in an image or a video and keep the usable ones as face regions. changes things detect-faces [-c <string>] [-f] [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to an image or video file. Option What it does -c <string> Minimum confidence (default: CFG_FACE_MIN_CONFIDENCE, 0.7) -f Re-detect: each face found continues the face-* region it is the same face as; manual-* boxes are kept. -v Verbose output. detect-faces /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg detect-faces /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0012.MP4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each face found, with its box and the crop written under the file; on a video, one per person told apart, with when it is on screen.

Find duplicate files by checksum (exact) or by fingerprint, copies with other bytes (--fuzzy); record the staged exact copies of files (--record), or look checksums up before an upload (--checksum) reads only duplicates [--fuzzy] [-t <string>] [-n <string>] [--min-count=<string>] [--min-size=<string>] [--against=<string>] [--record] [--checksum] <path>... Argument What it is <path>... file, subtree, or omit for the whole library; --record takes files and directories, --checksum checksums. Option What it does --fuzzy match fingerprints (resized, cropped, edited or rescanned copies) instead of checksums. -t <string> fuzzy similarity threshold (default 0.75 image / 0.80 video / 0.70 audio) -n <string> fuzzy: max results for a single file (default 20) --min-count=<string> exact: minimum copies to report a group (default 2) --min-size=<string> exact: ignore files smaller than this many bytes. --against=<string> exact: require copies in both the scoped subtree and this second root. --record decide again the duplicate findings of these staged files, of the staged copies of these library files, and of the files within these directories. --checksum the media originals you can read in the library or your own staging inbox that carry these checksums (at most 1000) duplicates /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 duplicates /home/anna/staging/files --against /archive/albums duplicates --fuzzy --min-count 2 /archive/albums duplicates --record /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-10-01/IMG_0001.jpg duplicates --checksum 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : groups of files that share a checksum, or with --fuzzy a fingerprint; --record: DuplicatesRecorded; --checksum: ChecksumMatches.

Birthdays, memorials and wedding anniversaries around a date, as events entries (core events gathers them) reads only events-anniversaries [--days-ahead=<number>] [--days-past=<number>] [--limit=<number>] [--today=<string>] [--people=<path>] Option What it does --days-ahead=<number> how far forward to look (default 30) --days-past=<number> how far back to look (default 7) --limit=<number> anniversaries returned; milestones survive the cut (default 16) --today=<string> the date to look around, YYYY-MM-DD (default today, UTC) --people=<path> people root to read (default /archive/people) events-anniversaries events-anniversaries --days-ahead 0 --days-past 0 events-anniversaries --today 2026-12-24 --days-ahead 7 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each birthday, milestone memorial and wedding anniversary in the window as an events entry, in date order: the day, the sentence, whether it is a milestone, the person, and the route that draws it.

Read what a file's metadata means in the archive: its capture time, resolved from its clocks, its camera, a paired sidecar and its name (a staged file by its category's time rules), and its position node from the GPS fix or the sidecar. changes things exif-interpret [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a file whose metadata is read (exif-extract) Option What it does -v Verbose output. exif-interpret /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the capture time it resolved and where, and its position; the attrs and the position node are written on the file.

Add a human-drawn face box to an image or a video frame as a new unidentified person. changes things face-add [--box=<string>] [--at=<string>] [--no-crop] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to an image or a video file. Option What it does --box=<string> display-frame fractions: x,y,width,height. --at=<string> on a video, required: the second of the frame the box is drawn on. --no-crop create the crop node without rendering it. face-add --box 0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg face-add --box 0.4,0.1,0.2,0.3 --at 12.5 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0012.mp4 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the new face and the unidentified person created for it.

Confirm that regions show the person they are assigned to. changes things face-confirm [--dry-run] <region>... Argument What it is <region>... region paths, /regions/ . Option What it does --dry-run check the regions without changing them. face-confirm /archive/photos/2001/IMG_0001.jpg/regions/face-0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the regions confirmed.

Question whether regions show the person they are assigned to. changes things face-doubt [--clear] [--dry-run] <region>... Argument What it is <region>... region paths, /regions/ . Option What it does --clear withdraw the doubt instead, leaving the person as it is. --dry-run check the regions without changing them. face-doubt /archive/photos/2001/IMG_0001.jpg/regions/face-0 face-doubt --clear /archive/photos/2001/IMG_0001.jpg/regions/face-0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the regions marked, or with --clear the regions cleared.

Remove a face and its person when it was the person's only unidentified face. changes things face-remove <face> Argument What it is <face> VFS path to a region. face-remove /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the face is removed.

Undo automatic face→person assignments by provenance, leaving manual ones intact. changes things face-reset [--source=<string>] [--delete-unnamed] [--dry-run] [--verbose] Option What it does --source=<string> auto | cluster | transfer | all (required) --delete-unnamed also delete every unnamed person. --dry-run report without changing anything. --verbose print each face. face-reset -- source cluster-faces --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many automatic assignments would be undone, by provenance.

Change a region's box and regenerate its preview crop; a moved face stops voting in recognition. changes things face-set-box [--box=<string>] [--no-crop] <face> Argument What it is <face> VFS path to a region. Option What it does --box=<string> display-frame fractions: x,y,width,height. --no-crop leave the crop bytes for regeneration. face-set-box --box 0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the box is changed and its crop regenerated.

Set a file's hand-written description. changes things file-set-description [--text=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. Option What it does --text=<string> the description; empty clears it, - reads it from stdin. file-set-description --text 'Ett exempel' /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0042.jpg cat notes.md | file-set-description --text - /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0042.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the description is written.

Rotate or mirror a file for good: writes angle/angleManual/mirror, remaps face boxes and regenerates renditions (a video re-encodes on the media pool) changes things file-set-orientation [--rotate=<string>] [--angle=<string>] [--mirror] [--toggle-mirror] [--no-regenerate] [-v] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. Option What it does --rotate=<string> relative turn: cw | ccw | 180. --angle=<string> absolute angle: 0 | 90 | 180 | 270. --mirror set the horizontal flip (--no-mirror clears it) --toggle-mirror flip the horizontal flip. --no-regenerate leave the still renditions and face crops stale (a video is still re-encoded on the media pool) -v verbose output. file-set-orientation --rotate 90 /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the file is rotated for good and its renditions regenerated.

Link the person who took a file (photographer softlink) changes things file-set-photographer <file> <person> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. <person> VFS path to person node. file-set-photographer /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg /archive/people/anna-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the photographer link is written.

Set a manual location override (positionManual + child position node) on a file, or clear its location. changes things file-set-position [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--clear] <file>... <lat> <lng> Argument What it is <file>... VFS paths to file nodes (several with --lat/--lng) <lat> latitude (positional; use --lat= if negative) <lng> longitude (positional; use --lng= if negative) Option What it does --lat=<string> latitude, as --lat= — required form for a negative coordinate. --lng=<string> longitude, as --lng= — required form for a negative coordinate. --clear take away the position and the location link instead of setting one. file-set-position /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg 59.0000 18.0000 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a manual location is written onto the file, or its location is taken away.

Set, annotate or clear a hand-typed capture time (whenManual) on one or more files. changes things file-set-time [--note=<string>] [--clear] <file> <when> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. <when> Capture time, YYYY[-MM[-DD[THH:MM[:SS]]]] (repeatable as file/time pairs) Option What it does --note=<string> Why this time is what it is — shown beside the date. --clear Remove the manual time and note, letting the exif-derived date win again. file-set-time /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg 2019-06-01T12:00 file-set-time --clear /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : FileSetTimeAnswer: each file with the capture time it now resolves to and its source.

Find positions inside a geographic bounding box: media points and locations. reads only find-within [--north=<string>] [--south=<string>] [--east=<string>] [--west=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--cursor=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--cell=<string>] [--include-hits] [--covers] [--facets] [--dir=<string>] [--person=<string>] [--location=<string>] [--tag=<string>] [-q <string>] [--under=<path>] Option What it does --north=<string> north edge latitude. --south=<string> south edge latitude. --east=<string> east edge longitude. --west=<string> west edge longitude. --limit=<string> page size (default: 100; with --cell, max points scanned, default 200000) --cursor=<string> resume after this row, from a previous answer's cursor. --from=<string> taken at/after this date (2020, 2020-05, 2020-05-01) --to=<string> taken before this date, exclusive (--to 2000 includes all of 2000) --cell=<string> cluster media into a grid of this many degrees and report counts. --include-hits with --cell, include members when the filtered answer has at most 500 media. --covers with --cell, give each cell of several pictures one of them as its cover. --facets answer with per-day, per-month and per-year counts instead of contents. --dir=<string> which way to page from the cursor: desc, asc (default desc, back in time) --person=<string> only media this person is tagged in (slug or path) --location=<string> only media linked to this location (slug or path) --tag=<string> only media carrying this label. -q <string> only media matching this text, searched inside the box. --under=<path> only media in this album or folder, as members lists it.

Import a GEDCOM file's people and relations: match each individual to a person of the archive or make one, add missing parents, partners, events, homes and descriptions, and keep the file in /archive/sources/genealogy, linked from every person it describes. changes things gedcom-import [--match=<string>] [--new=<string>] [--skip=<string>] [--dry-run] <file> Argument What it is <file> the GEDCOM (.ged) file. Option What it does --match=<string> who an individual is: ' = ', the person a path or a name under /archive/people (repeatable) --new=<string> make the individual with this xref a new person, whoever they fit (repeatable) --skip=<string> leave the individual with this xref, and their relations, out (repeatable) --dry-run say who would be matched, made and related, and what would be added, and write nothing. gedcom-import /home/ruby/wrenfield.ged --dry-run gedcom-import /home/ruby/wrenfield.ged gedcom-import /home/ruby/staging/genealogy/wrenfield.ged --match @I3@=ruby-wrenfield --new @I4@ --skip @I9@ With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the kept file, who each individual was found to be or was made, what was skipped, and how many relations, events and homes were added.

Read a GEDCOM file and say who each of its individuals would be if it were imported now: matched to a person, made one or left out, with the people who could be them. reads only gedcom-read [--match=<string>] [--new=<string>] [--skip=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> the GEDCOM (.ged) file. Option What it does --match=<string> who an individual is: ' = ', as gedcom-import takes it (repeatable) --new=<string> make the individual with this xref a new person (repeatable) --skip=<string> leave the individual with this xref out (repeatable) gedcom-read /home/ruby/staging/genealogy/wrenfield.ged gedcom-read /home/ruby/staging/genealogy/wrenfield.ged --match @I3@=ruby-wrenfield With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each individual with their names, dates and relatives in the file, whether they would be matched, made or left out, and their candidates; and the archive's people named, with their relatives.

Move a GEDCOM file staged under files/ to its staging area's genealogy/, where it waits to be looked over and imported. changes things gedcom-stage <file> Argument What it is <file> the staged GEDCOM (.ged) file. gedcom-stage /home/ruby/staging/files/inbox/upload-2026-11-01/wrenfield.ged With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : where the file waits, and how many individuals and families it holds.

Batch reverse geocode the position nodes of the files under a directory. changes things geocode-files [-r] [-f] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS directory path. Option What it does -r Recurse into subdirectories. -f Force re-geocode even if cached. -v Verbose output. geocode-files -r /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many position nodes were geocoded.

Resolve a location's written address to coordinates (Nominatim forward geocoding) changes things geocode-location [--force] [--dry-run] [--radius=<string>] [--countrycodes=<string>] [--query=<string>] [--verbose] [--accept=<number>] [--drawn] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a location (e.g. /archive/locations/ ) Option What it does --force Re-geocode even if already placed or attempted. --dry-run Report the query without calling the geocoder. --radius=<string> Radius in meters for the resulting circle (default 50) --countrycodes=<string> Restrict to these ISO country codes (default: se; empty to disable) --query=<string> Override the address text to look up. --verbose Print skipped locations too. --accept=<number> Take the geocoder's suggestion with this index (from the location's geocodeCandidates) instead of looking up; --radius sizes it. --drawn Record that the location's shape was drawn by hand, answering any pending review. geocode-location /archive/locations/Exempelstad geocode-location /archive/locations/Exempelstad --accept 0 --radius 150 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the coordinates the location's address resolved to.

Reverse geocode a file's position node using Nominatim (OSM) changes things geocode-position [-f] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a position node, /position. Option What it does -f Force re-geocode even if cached. -v Verbose output. geocode-position /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/position With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the address the coordinates resolved to.

Say what GPX files hold without importing them: size, name, description, time, creator, tracks, points and their time span, and the tracks of the devices each names. reads only gpx-info <gpx>... Argument What it is <gpx>... VFS paths to GPX files. gpx-info /home/anna/staging/routes/hike.gpx gpx-info /home/anna/staging/routes/*.gpx With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : one entry per file, in the order given; a file that could not be read gives its error instead.
Say hello (example TypeScript module command) reads only hello <name> Argument What it is <name> name to greet.

Learn labels from their pictures, so search --like /archive/tags/ can suggest where else they belong. reads only label-model [--all] [-v] [--if-stale] <subcommand> <label> <paths>... Argument What it is <subcommand> train | show | list | reject | unreject. <label> the label (train takes several) <paths>... reject, unreject: files or albums that are not the label. Option What it does --all train: every label in use, and every word of the vocabulary in the archive's language. -v train: report how long each phase took. --if-stale train: only labels whose members or rejections changed since they were trained, or that were trained more than a week ago. label-model train exempeletikett label-model train --all --if-stale label-model reject exempeletikett /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg search --like /archive/tags/exempeletikett --kind photo,video With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : for train , each label's LabelTrainResult; for show , the LabelModelSummary; for list , every kept model's LabelModelSummary; for reject and unreject , how many the label has rejected.

List the most recently captured media, newest first. reads only latest <count> Argument What it is <count> number of results (default 10, max 500) latest latest 20 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the most recently captured media, newest first, with capture time and dimensions.

Link geotagged media files to the location whose shape contains them ( /location softlink) changes things location-link-media [--location=<path>] [--point=<path>] [--root=<string>] [--dry-run] [--force] [--verbose] Option What it does --location=<path> only the files inside this location's shape, and those it no longer covers. --point=<path> only the file owning this /position node. --root=<string> media root to scan (default: /archive/albums) --dry-run report without creating or removing links. --force replace links made by hand or by the import too. --verbose print each link. location-link-media location-link-media --location /archive/locations/Exempelparken With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files were linked, unlinked, skipped and left outside every location.

List locations with their saved coordinates. reads only location-list [--without-coordinates] <root> Argument What it is <root> Location directory (default: /archive/locations) Option What it does --without-coordinates skip the position-registry scan.

Give a location coordinates from its linked media, falling back to geocoding its address. changes things location-locate [--all] [--root=<string>] [--limit=<string>] [--min-points=<string>] [--max-spread=<string>] [--radius=<string>] [--no-geocode] [--force] [--refresh] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a location (e.g. /archive/locations/ ); omit with --all. Option What it does --all Process every location under --root. --root=<string> Locations root (default: /archive/locations) --limit=<string> Stop after this many locations. --min-points=<string> Fewest geotagged files a centroid may rest on (default 2) --max-spread=<string> Reject a centroid whose media spread wider than this, in meters (default 25000) --radius=<string> Fixed radius in meters, instead of one derived from the media spread. --no-geocode Centroid only — never fall back to the address geocoder. --force Re-locate locations that already have a shape. --refresh Re-derive a placed location too, writing only what moved; never touches coordinates set by hand. --dry-run Report what would be applied without writing anything. --verbose Print each location.

Turn a location name (a city, a country, an area) into the region search --bbox filters on. reads only location-region [--countrycodes=<string>] [--bbox-only] <name>... Argument What it is <name>... the location as the user named it, in any language. Option What it does --countrycodes=<string> limit the match to these countries, comma-separated ISO codes (se,no) --bbox-only print only the box, for search --bbox=$(…) location-region Exempelstad search --bbox=$(location-region Exempelstad --bbox-only) --group-by album With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the location's full name and its bounding box as north,south,east,west — the form search --bbox= takes.

What happened at one location as a chronological feed: residents moving in and out, its events and the albums with photos from it. reads only location-timeline [--no-albums] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to location node. Option What it does --no-albums skip the albums, which are most of the cost. location-timeline /archive/locations/ekbacksvagen With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the location's history in order: moves in and out, its events and the albums with photos taken there.

Change a location's name, address, description, city or country. changes things location-update [--name=<string>] [--address=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--city=<string>] [--country=<string>] [--clear=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to location node. Option What it does --name=<string> what the location is called; a name given here is never looked up again (track-places --rename) --address=<string> the written address; a change is geocoded again by location-upkeep. --description=<string> free text about the location. --city=<string> city. --country=<string> country. --clear=<string> remove a field (repeatable): address, description, city or country. location-update /archive/locations/ekbacksvagen --address 'Ekbacksvägen 4, 123 45 Exempelby' location-update /archive/locations/ekbacksvagen --clear description With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : which fields changed.

Read description, time, location, camera with owners, albums, tagged people (with age), comments and versions for a media file. reads only media-details [--album=<path>] [--fields=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to file node. Option What it does --album=<path> album context for stack membership and exclusion details. --fields=<string> extra fields to include: raw (the full exiftool dump) media-details /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the file's description, when and where it was taken, its albums, the people in it with their ages, and its versions.

Start a pass of media-scan over the albums or a staging area when one is due, and none while a pass runs. changes things media-heal [--rest=<number>] [-n] Option What it does --rest=<number> Seconds after a pass that found nothing before the next (default CFG_MEDIA_HEAL_REST, else 21600) -n Dry run — say whether a pass is due without announcing it. media-heal -n media-heal --rest 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : whether a pass was announced, and why or why not.

Re-resolve media originals' capture times from their stored exif and manual sources. changes things media-resolve-time [--dry-run] [--under=<path>] [--camera=<path>] [-v] Option What it does --dry-run report what would change, write nothing. --under=<path> only the files in the tree under this directory or album, or this one file. --camera=<path> only files linked to this camera (its cameraPath) -v print every file that changes. media-resolve-time --dry-run media-resolve-time --under /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 media-resolve-time --camera /archive/cameras/Exempelkamera --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files had their capture time re-resolved, and from which source.

Emit media events for files the bridge never saw (backfill / gap recovery) changes things media-scan [--limit=<number>] [--max-active=<number>] [--depth=<number>] [--scan-limit=<number>] [--restart] [--no-gaps] [--if-idle] [--only=<string>] [-n] [-v] <root> Argument What it is <root> Subtree to scan (default /archive/albums) Option What it does --limit=<number> Maximum events to emit per run; 0 emits every gap found (default 1000) --max-active=<number> Cap running media-ingest instances plus queued triggers; 0 adds no cap (default 500) --depth=<number> Maximum directory depth (default 12) --scan-limit=<number> Maximum files examined per run; 0 walks the whole subtree (default 20000) --restart Ignore the stored resume point and start the pass at the top. --no-gaps Only discover unindexed files; skip half-indexed ones. --if-idle Hold back the facts whose pipelines have work ready, in the trigger pool or the media pool, and name them; scan nothing when all wait, or when EMS cannot be asked what it runs now. --only=<string> Emit only these fact types, comma-separated (e.g. media.faces.stale); the cursor still moves, so follow with a --restart pass for the rest. -n Dry run — report what would be emitted. -v Verbose output. media-scan /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 media-scan -- limit 500 /archive/albums media-scan --only media.faces.stale --scan-limit 0 /archive/albums With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files were announced to the media pipeline.

Pair the Google Photos Takeout JSON and XMP sidecars in a folder with their files, as /sidecar, and carry over their dates, places, captions and favourites. changes things media-sidecars [--dry-run] <folder> Argument What it is <folder> the folder whose sidecars are paired, at any depth; the working directory when none is given. Option What it does --dry-run count what would be paired and carried over, changing nothing. media-sidecars /home/anna/staging/files/google-photos/upload-2026-10-18 media-sidecars '/home/anna/staging/files/google-photos/Takeout/Google Photos/Sommar i Exempelstad' --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : MediaSidecarsAnswer: the sidecars found, paired, shared and unmatched, and what the files were given.

List an album's media by the album's own rules: an imported album's files/ folder, links followed, the cover left out, stacks of similar photos folded. reads only members-album [--include-stacked] <album> Argument What it is <album> album path. Option What it does --include-stacked text output: also list the photos folded under a stack. members-album /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 members-album /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 --include-stacked With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every member, stacked ones included: its path, node id, the link it is a member through, and for a stacked photo the front that stands for it and the stack size.

Keep one file of a set of duplicates, fill it in from the others, and move them to the trash as one batch. changes things merge-duplicates [--batch=<string>] [--label=<string>] [--dry-run] <keep> <drop>... Argument What it is <keep> the file kept. <drop>... the duplicates dropped into the trash. Option What it does --batch=<string> trash into this batch (an id from trash put --batch), or with no id a new one. --label=<string> what the batch is called in the trash. --dry-run say what would be filled in and trashed, changing nothing. merge-duplicates /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0001.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/IMG_0001.jpg merge-duplicates --label 'Copies of a sailboat' /archive/albums/Exempelalbum/files/IMG_0002.jpg /home/anna/staging/files/inbox/IMG_0002.jpg --dry-run With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : MergeDuplicatesResult: the fields filled in, how many were trashed, and the batch that trash restore takes back.

Recently created albums, newest first, with who made them, as news entries (core news gathers them) reads only news-albums [--limit=<number>] [--preview=<number>] [--albums=<path>] Option What it does --limit=<number> albums returned (default 8) --preview=<number> pictures kept per album (default 5) --albums=<path> album root to read (default /archive/albums) news-albums news-albums -- limit 20 --preview 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the newest albums by creation time as news entries: when, who made it, a title, the album, and the route that draws it with the member count and a few pictures.

The years with pictures taken on a day (MM-DD, default today), as onthisday entries (core onthisday gathers them) reads only onthisday-media [--limit=<number>] [<day>] Argument What it is [<day>] day as MM-DD (default today, UTC) Option What it does --limit=<number> years returned, newest first (default 8) onthisday-media onthisday-media 06-21 -- limit 20 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : one onthisday entry per year with pictures taken on that day, newest year first: the year, a title, the year's first picture, and the route that draws it as a ring.

Score the search parse (archive-parse) against the filters each question means. reads only parse-eval [--questions=<path>] [--limit=<number>] Option What it does --questions=<path> a JSON array of {text, people, locations, from, to}. --limit=<number> stop after this many questions. parse-eval --questions /tmp/parse-questions.json With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : per question: people, locations and years right of those asked for, names made up, and the time; totals and p50/p90.

People and family tree management. person <subcommand> Argument What it is <subcommand> Subcommand: list, create, name, merge, detach, discard, unknown, faces, set-parent, set-partner, remove, add-event, info, children, family-tree, graph, timeline, how-related, check, fixup. person info /archive/people/anna-exempel person create /archive/people/cecilia-exempel --name 'Cecilia Exempel' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : whatever the subcommand answers with; 'person' alone lists the subcommands.

Add an event (blob) to a person, album, location or camera. changes things person-add-event [--type=<string>] [--date=<string>] [--qualifier=<string>] [--body=<string>] [--lat=<string>] [--lng=<string>] [--writer=<path>] <target> [<name>] Argument What it is <target> VFS path to the person, album, location or camera. [<name>] optional event name (e.g. birth, wedding); without one, it is made from the type and date. Option What it does --type=<string> event type: birth, death, marriage, engagement, generic; a dated birth/death also sets born/died. --date=<string> event date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --qualifier=<string> the date is about, before or after the day it names: about, before or after; a birth/death sets the same on born/died. --body=<string> event body text (markdown); - reads it from stdin. --lat=<string> latitude for the event position node. --lng=<string> longitude for the event position node. --writer=<path> the person who wrote the text, linked as the event's writer ; without it, whoever adds the event. person-add-event -- date 1998-06 --body 'Flyttade till Lund' /archive/people/anna-exempel person-add-event -- type marriage -- date 1972-05-20 /archive/people/anna-exempel wedding person-add-event -- date 2019-07-14 --body 'A day on the water' --writer /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the event path; the event is written, and for a dated birth/death the born/died attr.

Check family-tree integrity (dangling links, reciprocity, cycles, dates, birth/death events not on born/died) reads only person-check [--json] <root> Argument What it is <root> people root (default /archive/people) Option What it does --json JSON output. person-check /archive/people With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every dangling link, missing reciprocal, cycle, impossible date and birth/death event not mirrored onto born/died it found.

List a person's children (children/ dir) reads only person-children <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. person-children /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each child's name and slug.

Give a named person without a cover the crop of one of their own faces (coverPhoto softlink) changes things person-cover [--all] [--file=<path>] [--repick] [--limit=<number>] [--verbose] <person> Argument What it is <person> person path (repeatable) Option What it does --all every named person. --file=<path> the people whose faces are in this image. --repick choose again over a cover this command picked earlier; never over one somebody set. --limit=<number> stop after this many people. --verbose print each person as it is written. person-cover /archive/people/anna-exempel person-cover --file /archive/media/2019/IMG_0001.jpg person-cover --all -- limit 50 person-cover --all --repick With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; a coverPhoto softlink to a face crop is written for each named person that had no usable cover.

Create a person node. changes things person-create [--name=<string>] [--fullname=<string>] [--gender=<string>] [--born=<string>] [--died=<string>] [--allergies=<string>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path for the person node. Option What it does --name=<string> , -n Display name. --fullname=<string> , -f Full name. --gender=<string> , -g Gender: male, female, other, unknown. --born=<string> , -b Birth date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --died=<string> , -d Death date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --allergies=<string> , -a Allergy notes. person-create /archive/people/disa-exempel --name 'Disa Exempel' --born 2019-01-01 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the person node is created.

Take faces off a person: to a new unnamed person, to an existing one, or off identity entirely. changes things person-detach [--to=<string>] [--to-new-person] [--rematch] [--dry-run] [--verbose] <facePath...> Argument What it is <facePath...> regions or voices, e.g. /albums/x.jpg/regions/face-0. Option What it does --to=<string> move the faces to this person (path or bare unknown id) --to-new-person mint one unnamed person and move the faces there. --rematch not this person: let recognition place each face again, never back on the person it left. --dry-run report what would move without changing anything. --verbose print each face. person-detach --rematch /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 person-detach --to-new-person /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg/regions/face-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : which faces moved, and to whom, and the unnamed people left empty and removed.

Say unidentified people are not a person at all: unassign and lock everything they hold, and remove them. changes things person-discard [--dry-run] <person...> Argument What it is <person...> unnamed people, by path or bare unknown id. Option What it does --dry-run report what would go without changing anything. person-discard /archive/people/unknown/01J0EXAMPLE person-discard --dry-run 01J0EXAMPLE 01J0EXAMPLF With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the people removed, with how many regions and voices each let go, and the ones refused.

Every face and tag assigned to a person, with the photo each came from. reads only person-faces [--limit=<string>] [--offset=<string>] [--sort=<string>] [--doubtful] <person> Argument What it is <person> person path, or a bare id under /archive/people/unknown. Option What it does --limit=<string> max faces to return (default: all as text, 500 as JSON) --offset=<string> skip this many (default 0) --sort=<string> 'confidence' (default), 'file', chronological 'date', or 'doubt' (the ones a person asked about, then the clearest) --doubtful only the faces in question: questioned by somebody, or found looking like somebody else. person-faces /archive/people/anna-exempel person-faces -- limit 20 -- sort date /archive/people/anna-exempel person-faces --doubtful -- sort doubt /archive/people/anna-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the faces assigned to the person, with the photo each came from; JSON pages, and nextOffset starts the next page.

Display ancestors and descendants of a person. reads only person-family-tree [--up=<number>] [--down=<number>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --up=<number> ancestor generations (default 3) --down=<number> descendant generations (default 2) person-family-tree --up 2 --down 2 /archive/people/anna-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the person's ancestors and descendants to the given depth.

Repair family-tree links (recreate missing reciprocals, rewrite stale reciprocal paths, drop dangling) changes things person-fixup [--dry-run=<string>] [--delete-orphans] <root> Argument What it is <root> people root (default /archive/people) Option What it does --dry-run=<string> report without changing. --delete-orphans delete unnamed people left with no faces. person-fixup --dry-run /archive/people With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : which family links would be recreated, rewritten or dropped; exits 1 when a person could not be repaired.

Family graph around a person as nodes and edges, for drawing a tree. reads only person-graph [--up=<number>] [--down=<number>] [--only=<path>] [--to=<path>] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --up=<number> ancestor generations (default 2, max 8) --down=<number> descendant generations (default 2, max 8) --only=<path> draw only the person and these people, no walk (repeatable) --to=<path> draw the line of relations from the person to this one: how the two are related (repeatable) person-graph --up 2 --down 2 /archive/people/anna-exempel person-graph /archive/people/anna-exempel --only /archive/people/bo-exempel --only /archive/people/cecilia-exempel person-graph /archive/people/anna-exempel --to /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the family graph around the person as nodes and edges, for drawing.

Compute the kinship term between two persons (English/Swedish) reads only person-how-related [--lang=<string>] [--json] <a> <b> Argument What it is <a> first person. <b> second person. Option What it does --lang=<string> en|sv (default $CFG_LANGUAGE or en) --json JSON output. person-how-related /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/people/bo-exempel person-how-related --lang sv /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the kinship term in English and Swedish, as a sentence to repeat as it comes.

Show person details, relationships, and events. reads only person-info <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. person-info /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the person's name, birth and death dates, their parents, partners and children, and their events.

List the named people, with how many files of the library each is seen or heard in. reads only person-list [--sort=<string>] [--limit=<number>] [--min=<number>] Option What it does --sort=<string> name (default; placeholder names last) or count (most pictured first) --limit=<number> at most this many people. --min=<number> only people in at least this many files. With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the named people with the number of files each is in, as JSON (PersonListEntry[]).

Merge people into another (faces, events, relations and links to them move; the sources are removed) changes things person-merge [--dry-run] [--force] [--verbose] <src...> <dst> Argument What it is <src...> people to merge away. <dst> person to keep. Option What it does --dry-run report what would move without changing anything. --force merge even if a source has children this cannot move. --verbose print detail. person-merge /archive/people/unnamed-1 /archive/people/anna-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : what moved; with --dry-run, what would move.

Name an unidentified person and move them into /people. changes things person-name [--name=<string>] [--slug=<string>] [--fullname=<string>] [--birthname=<string>] [--gender=<string>] [--born=<string>] [--died=<string>] <person> Argument What it is <person> path (or bare id) of an unnamed person. Option What it does --name=<string> display name (required) --slug=<string> path segment (default: derived from the name) --fullname=<string> full name. --birthname=<string> name at birth. --gender=<string> male, female, other, unknown. --born=<string> birth date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --died=<string> death date (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) person-name --name 'Anna Exempel' --born 1970-01-01 /archive/people/unnamed-1 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the named person and their new path under /archive/people.

Who a kin phrase reaches from a person through the family tree: 'moster', 'mammas syster', 'barn', 'my father's brother'. reads only person-relatives [--relation=<string>] [--age=<number>] <person> Argument What it is <person> the person to start from: a VFS path, or a slug under the people root. Option What it does --relation=<string> kin word or chain in Swedish or English, as the user said it. --age=<number> also give the capture-date span in which each relative was this many years old. person-relatives /archive/people/anna-exempel --relation moster person-relatives anna-exempel --relation 'mammas syster' person-relatives anna-exempel --relation dotter --age 6 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : each relative the phrase reaches, with their path, name, birth and death dates and what they are to the person in Swedish and English; with --age, the capture-date span to search in.

Remove a relationship between two persons (both sides) changes things person-remove <a> <b> Argument What it is <a> first person. <b> second person. person-remove /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the relation is removed from both sides.

Remove a person↔location residence relation (both halves) changes things person-remove-home <person> <location> Argument What it is <person> VFS path to person node. <location> VFS path to a location. person-remove-home /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/locations/Exempelstad With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the residence relation is removed from both sides.

Record where a person lived, and when (dated relation pair) changes things person-set-home [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] [--update] <person> <location> Argument What it is <person> VFS path to person node. <location> VFS path to a location. Option What it does --from=<string> moved in (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --to=<string> moved out (YYYY[-MM[-DD]]) --update rewrite the span of a residence that already exists; the flags given are the new span. person-set-home --from 2001-01 /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/locations/Exempelstad With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the residence relation is written on both sides.

Add a parent relationship (parents/ ↔ children/) changes things person-set-parent [--kind=<string>] <child> <parent> Argument What it is <child> VFS path of the child person. <parent> VFS path of the parent person. Option What it does --kind=<string> blood (default) | adoptive | step | foster. person-set-parent /archive/people/cecilia-exempel /archive/people/anna-exempel person-set-parent --kind adoptive /archive/people/disa-exempel /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the link is written.

Add or update a partner relationship (partners/, both directions) changes things person-set-partner [--kind=<string>] [--from=<string>] [--to=<string>] <a> <b> Argument What it is <a> VFS path of first person. <b> VFS path of second person. Option What it does --kind=<string> partner (default) | married. --from=<string> partnership start date. --to=<string> partnership end date. person-set-partner --kind married --from 2001-01-01 /archive/people/anna-exempel /archive/people/bo-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the link is written in both directions.

Count births, engagements, marriages and deaths by calendar month across all years. reads only person-stats person-stats With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : months (twelve rows of counts per kind), totals, and withoutMonth for dates known only to the year.

One person's life as a chronological feed: events, homes, partnerships, children and albums. reads only person-timeline [--no-albums] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to person node. Option What it does --no-albums skip the albums, which are most of the cost — the life itself in a few round trips. person-timeline /archive/people/anna-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the person's life in order: events, homes, partnerships, children and the albums they appear in.

List auto-created people nobody has named yet, with face counts and crops. reads only person-unknown [--limit=<string>] [--offset=<string>] [--faces=<string>] [--sort=<string>] [--min-faces=<string>] [--person=<string>] Option What it does --limit=<string> max people to return (default 200) --offset=<string> skip this many (default 0) --faces=<string> crops per person (default 4) --sort=<string> 'faces' (default) or 'created'. --min-faces=<string> only people with at least this many faces and recordings together. --person=<string> return one person by node id or path. person-unknown -- limit 20 -- sort faces person-unknown -- sort created --min-faces 5 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : auto-created people nobody has named, with their face counts and crops; JSON pages, and nextOffset starts the next page.

Change a person's profile: names, birth and death dates, gender, allergies, description, contact details. An empty value clears the field. changes things person-update [--name=<string>] [--fullname=<string>] [--birthname=<string>] [--born=<string>] [--died=<string>] [--born-qualifier=<string>] [--died-qualifier=<string>] [--gender=<string>] [--allergies=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--contact=<string>] <person> Argument What it is <person> the person. Option What it does --name=<string> the name shown everywhere (cannot be empty) --fullname=<string> full name. --birthname=<string> name at birth. --born=<string> birth date, YYYY[-MM[-DD]]. --died=<string> death date, YYYY[-MM[-DD]]. --born-qualifier=<string> the birth date is about, before or after the day given: about, before or after; --born alone clears it. --died-qualifier=<string> the death date is about, before or after the day given: about, before or after; --died alone clears it. --gender=<string> male, female, other or unknown. --allergies=<string> allergy notes. --description=<string> a few words about the person. --contact=<string> contact details as a JSON list of { "type", "data" }. person-update /archive/people/Anna_Andersson --born=1970-01-01 --died= '' person-update /archive/people/Anna_Andersson --born=1890 --born-qualifier=about person-update /archive/people/Anna_Andersson --contact '[{"type":"email","data":"anna@example.com"}]' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the fields given are written, empty ones cleared.

Every recording a person is heard in, with how long they speak and a moment to hear them. reads only person-voices [--limit=<string>] [--offset=<string>] [--sort=<string>] <person> Argument What it is <person> person path, or a bare id under /archive/people/unknown. Option What it does --limit=<string> max voices to return (default: all) --offset=<string> skip this many (default 0) --sort=<string> 'duration' (most spoken first, default), 'file', or chronological 'date'. person-voices /archive/people/anna-exempel With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : every recording voice assigned to the person, with its talk time and the moment to play.

Detect RAW image files and report (or --sort) the non-RAW file(s) they are related to. reads only raw [--sort] [-n <string>] [--unmatched] [-v] <path> Argument What it is <path> file, album, subtree, or omit for the whole library. Option What it does --sort move each RAW under the versions/ dir of its partner of the same name, and delete its regions; a RAW with no such partner is left as is. On a non-RAW file, sort its RAWs under it. -n <string> max partner candidates per file (default 5) --unmatched scan: list only RAW files with no partner found. -v verbose output. raw /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/DSC_0001.NEF raw -- sort /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the non-RAW files the RAW is related to; with --sort, what became of each RAW.
