Turn an automation off: a person's by whoever may change its file, a module's by the administrator. changes things automation-disable <automation> Argument What it is <automation> , / , or its file. automation-disable hall-light

Turn an automation on: a person's by whoever may change its file, a module's by the administrator. changes things automation-enable <automation> Argument What it is <automation> , / , or its file. automation-enable hall-light

Run the automations under /etc/automations and /etc/automations.d when a reading, a press, a device coming or going or the clock says so, each as its owner (the automation-engine service) administrators only · changes things automation-engine service restart automation-engine

The devices on the network the network listener heard over mDNS, SSDP and WS-Discovery: what each is, whether it can become a device and whether it is one already (for members of the devices group) reads only automation-found [--addable] [--all] [<id>] Argument What it is [<id>] one host, by its id or address: it, with all the listener heard of it. Option What it does --addable only the ones that can become a device of automation’s. --all every one, the devices already under /dev and the ignored ones too. automation-found automation-found --addable automation-found --all automation-found 7c2ebd614055 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : FoundAnswer: round, broker, devices [{id, ip, mac, names, seen, services, kind, vendor, label, model, firmware, class, addable, adopt, connect, device, ignored}]; with an id, FoundDetail: one of those and host {ip, mac, names, seen, mdns, ssdp}.

Leave devices found on the network out of automation-found, or take them back with --undo (for members of the devices group) changes things automation-ignore [--undo] <id> Argument What it is <id> what automation-found calls it; more than one may be given. Option What it does --undo take them back. automation-ignore d0ad08c5e709 automation-ignore d0ad08c5e709 --undo

Make an automation under /etc/automations, empty or from a starting point with its slots set to your devices; one with slots set is checked, and refused with problems (members of the automation group) changes things automation-new [--from=<string>] [--set=<string>] [--description=<string>] [--dry-run] [--examples] <name> Argument What it is <name> its name: letters, digits, ., - and _. Option What it does --from=<string> a starting point: empty, motion-light, button-toggle, heater, morning, inbox, dusk-to-dawn, tour. --set=<string> a slot of the starting point, = : an endpoint as / , none to leave an optional one out; --examples lists them. --description=<string> what it does, a sentence (the starting point says it when not given) --dry-run write nothing: say what is wrong with it, and in text the YAML it would write. --examples list the starting points and their slots. automation-new hall-light --from motion-light automation-new hall-light --from motion-light -- set motion=hall-sensor/motion -- set lamp=hall-lamp/switch-0 -- set light-level=none --dry-run automation-new --examples With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutomationSetAnswer: name, path, written, created, problems.

Write an automation's YAML, made when it is new; one with problems is refused unless --draft. changes things automation-set [--yaml=<string>] [--json=<string>] [--draft] [--dry-run] <automation> Argument What it is <automation> or its file. Option What it does --yaml=<string> the YAML, written as given. --json=<string> its graph as JSON, written as YAML. --draft write it even with problems, unless it is not YAML; it is not run until they are gone. --dry-run write nothing: say what is wrong with it as automation-check does, devices you may not read or switch among it. automation-set hall-light < hall-light.yaml automation-set hall-light --yaml " $text " --draft With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutomationSetAnswer: name, path, written, created, problems.

An automation's YAML, whose it is, whether it runs and what is wrong with it; in JSON mode also its graph with every node placed. reads only automation-show <automation> Argument What it is <automation> , / , or its file. automation-show hall-light With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutomationDetail: name, path, module, owner, description, enabled, running, nodes, problems, writable, text, spec.

Walk a device's SNMP objects under an OID (the system group unless one is given), for members of the devices group. reads only automation-snmp [--community=<string>] [--port=<string>] [--limit=<string>] <host> [<oid>] Argument What it is <host> its address. [<oid>] where to walk from: 1.3.6.1.2.1.1 unless given. Option What it does --community=<string> the community to ask with, when not CFG_AUTOMATION_SNMP_COMMUNITY. --port=<string> its agent’s port, when not 161. --limit=<string> the most objects to answer (5000) automation-snmp 192.0.2.40 automation-snmp 192.0.2.40 1.3.6.1.2.1.25.2.3 automation-snmp 192.0.2.40 1.3.6.1.4.1.4526 --community home With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : SnmpObject[]: oid, type, value.

Whether the automation bridge hears the MQTT broker, which drivers it registered, how many devices under /dev they drive, what they cannot read, and the automations; or, given one, what each of its nodes last did. reads only automation-status [--brief] [--checks] [--automations] [<automation>] Argument What it is [<automation>] one automation, whose nodes to show. Option What it does --brief one line, as the services list shows it. --checks the checks health reads, as JSON. --automations one line on the automation engine, as the services list shows it. automation-status automation-status --brief automation-status hall-light With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutomationStatus: configured, url, running, connected, since, drivers, devices, endpoints, messages, unsupported, lastError, automations {running, actions, problems}; with an automation, AutomationRunStatus: name, running, problems, nodes.

Press a button node of a running automation: what it is wired to runs now, as its owner. changes things automation-trigger <automation> <node> Argument What it is <automation> , / , or its file. <node> the button node. automation-trigger hall-light try-it

The automations, whose each is, whether it runs, and what is wrong with those that do not. reads only automations automations With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : AutomationSummary[]: name, path, module, owner, description, enabled, running, nodes, problems, writable.

The Media module reads every picture, video and recording as it arrives, and makes the thumbnails, display sizes and playable copies of each in a folder that wants them, the picture vectors that search finds a picture by what it shows, the text in pictures and documents, and what is said in videos and recordings, and keeps the renditions and picture vectors current. It also runs the media work the other modules hand it, so that a large import never starts it all at once: with the Archive , dating and placing each file, and finding and matching faces and voices. It holds the workers of the pool that work waits in, and their settings. The Archive and Recipes need it, so it comes with either.
Installing the Archive or Recipes installs it too. On its own: # in EiN's terminal, as the administrator mod install media Modules covers installing and removing modules.

When a picture, video or recording has its last byte written, the media-bridge service announces it, and media-ingest reads it with exif-extract , through the media service . What it reads goes on the file: its type, its size and shape, how it is turned, and a video's or recording's length and codec. Everything the file's metadata says is kept under it, as metadata/exif : the camera that made it, the clocks it recorded, and its GPS fix. What these mean, such as when the picture was taken and where, the other modules work out: the Archive's way is in Dates and places . The renditions and every other module's work on the file wait for the reading. When a file's bytes change, media-reindex reads it again. Nothing under /tmp , /etc , /var , /usr or /dev is read, nor anything in a trash, nor a rendition. A video or recording whose container cannot be read is marked undecodable , and nothing is made of it. A module can hold a file before it is read. A held file is left unread, and nothing starts for it, for as long as it has the same bytes in the same folder. The Archive holds a file that arrives in a staging area as an exact copy of one its owner already has ( An exact copy shows its original ). You want to Run Read a file again, also one held or marked undecodable exif-extract -f /archive/albums/christmas-2019/IMG_0042.jpg See everything its metadata says attrs /archive/albums/christmas-2019/IMG_0042.jpg/metadata/exif

The thumbnails, display sizes, video and sound copies are listed in /etc/renditions.yaml , each under the role it plays: thumb , the square thumbnail, and grid , small , medium and large , which keep the picture's shape; a video's preview , the silent clip a tile plays, and its playback ; a recording's playback ; and the storyboard , a video's frames on one sheet. A picture role's kinds says what it is made of: photo , video , audio (the waveform) and document (a document's first page). A file from before documents got pictures has no document in its kinds, and documents get no picture until it is added. The pages ask for a role, so changing a size there changes what they show. renditions in the terminal says what the file holds now, and names any entry it leaves out as wrong. Two pipelines make them, once a file's metadata is read: media-stills the pictures (a photo's sizes, a video's poster frames and then its hover clip, a recording's waveform, and as soon as a document is written its first page, with the PDF of a Word, OpenDocument or RTF file, view.pdf , which the viewer shows), and media-transcode the video and sound a browser can play, with a video's storyboard and its chapters, the cuts its player marks. A folder whose processing setting leaves out renditions gets none ( Which processing a folder wants ). The Media module installed the file, and a newer version of it never overwrites it, so a change you make stays. Each rendition is named after its size ( 800x800.avif ), so a size changed is a new file for every picture. Pages pick up the change when they are opened again.

Once a file has every rendition /etc/renditions.yaml names for it, it is marked with the table they were made by ( renditionsFor and renditionsAt in its attributes). Every hour the renditions-heal service runs renditions-scan , which asks for the files whose mark is missing or names another table, in every folder that wants renditions, and announces them to media-stills and media-transcode , which make what is missing. A size changed in the table is made for every file of the kinds it touched, which on a large archive takes hours or days. A rendition the media service refused for its processor budget counts as made, until that budget changes. While rendition work waits, the scan announces nothing, so it never repeats what is already on its way. You want to Run See which files lack renditions the table names, without changing anything renditions-scan -n -v Announce them now, rather than at the next hour renditions-scan Make the renditions again under a folder, without the pipelines regenerate --force /archive/albums/christmas-2019 Remove the renditions no role names any more regenerate --prune /archive Media commands lists their options.

A photo, and each keyframe of a video, gets a picture vector: what the media service's picture model sees in it, which search compares with the words you type, so a picture is found by what it shows without a caption. media-embed-picture makes them once a file is read, in a folder that wants picture-vectors ( Which processing a folder wants ), and marks the file with the model that made them. Every hour the pictures-heal service runs pictures-scan , which asks for the photos and videos whose mark is missing or names another model than the media service runs now, in every folder that wants them, and announces them to media-embed-picture . Vectors the model in use made are kept and the file marked; another model's are made again, so when the media service changes its picture model the whole archive is embedded again, behind all other work. While picture work waits, the scan announces nothing. You want to Run See which files lack picture vectors from the model in use pictures-scan -n -v Announce them now, rather than at the next hour pictures-scan Make a file's picture vectors again, whatever model made them embed-picture -f /archive/albums/christmas-2019/IMG_0042.jpg

A picture, each keyframe of a video, and a recording get a fingerprint: a description made to find copies whatever their bytes, a picture saved smaller or in another format, mildly cropped or turned, a video or recording encoded again. The Archive compares them to find duplicates, look-alikes and the photos of a burst. media-fingerprint makes them once a file is read, in a folder that wants fingerprints ( Which processing a folder wants ), and marks the file once they are all there. A recording shorter than about two and a half seconds has too little sound for one, and is marked all the same. Every hour the fingerprints-heal service runs fingerprints-scan , which asks for the pictures, videos and recordings without the mark, in every folder that wants them, and announces them to media-fingerprint : a file whose fingerprints are all there is only marked, the others get theirs. While fingerprint work waits, the scan announces nothing. You want to Run See which files were never fingerprinted to the end fingerprints-scan -n -v Announce them now, rather than at the next hour fingerprints-scan Fingerprint a file again compute-fingerprint -f /archive/albums/christmas-2019/IMG_0042.jpg

In a folder that wants text , the text written in a picture is read once the picture is ( media-ocr , read-text ), and a PDF, plain text, Word or OpenDocument text file's text once its last byte is written ( document-index , index-document ); nothing is read while it is in a staging area. In a folder that wants transcripts , what is said in a video or recording is written as its transcript ( media-transcribe , transcribe-file ). Each text gets a vector, which search finds it by. A person corrects them in the viewer , with file-set-text , file-set-text-language and file-set-transcript underneath; the voices in a transcript, and who speaks, are the Archive's.

A file is marked with what made its transcript and its text vectors ( transcriptWith and textVectorsBy in its attributes), as it is with the engine that read its text ( ocrBy ). Every hour the text-heal service runs text-scan , which asks, in every folder that wants them, for: a video or recording whose transcript is missing or was made with other speech settings than the media service runs now, announced to media-transcribe . A transcript made with the settings in use is kept and the file marked; one made with others is made again, so a change of the media service's speech settings transcribes the whole archive again, behind all other work. One a person wrote, and one of a file with no sound, is kept whatever the settings. a picture whose text another engine read, announced to media-ocr , unless a person wrote it. a picture or document whose text was never read, announced to media-ocr or document-index . A folder moved in whole has its files' text read the same way, as soon as it arrives. a file whose texts lack vectors from the text model the media service runs now, announced to media-embed-text . A description changed by hand is embedded again as soon as it is saved. Each kind of gap waits while its work waits, so the scan never repeats what is already on its way, and a check that needs the media service is left out while it does not answer. Nothing in a staging area is asked about its text: it is read when the file is filed. Keep transcripts current ( CFG_MEDIA_TRANSCRIPTS_CURRENT ) set to off leaves the transcripts there are alone, when a change of speech settings should not mean hours of background work: only a file with no mark is asked about, and what it has is kept. You want to Run See which files have text, transcripts or vectors to catch up text-scan -n -v Announce them now, rather than at the next hour text-scan Read the text in a picture again read-text -f /archive/albums/christmas-2019/IMG_0042.jpg Read a document's text again index-document -f /home/helen/letters/1962.pdf Transcribe a video or recording again, whatever made its words transcribe-file -f /archive/albums/christmas-2019/MVI_0412.mp4 Embed every stored text and transcript again, as they are media-reembed

The Media module makes a picture's restored copies, through the media service : file-restore restores one while someone waits, and file-restore --queue many in the background, each picture's request kept on it until media-restore has made its copy, as the restore kind of the models worker. find-damage reads how faded, dusty, scratched, blurred and shaken a picture is and keeps it on the file, where search --has damage=faded finds it; the Archive runs it on its scans ( Find the scans worth restoring ).

Each module puts the work a crawl must not start all at once as jobs into the pool /var/pools/media , and names the kinds of its jobs for the workers here: media-worker runs the work that is not a model request, on one budget of the processor's slots. models keeps the model requests in flight against the media service , and rotates between their kinds, so that faces do not starve the rest. models-second , off unless CFG_MODEL_SECOND_SLOTS is above 0, takes the same kinds in the reverse order, so the media service runs a second family of models beside the first. With more than one media service , models and media-worker run a worker for each other instance beside their own, named models@laptop and media-worker@laptop , with the kinds that instance serves; media-pool-kinds models --instance laptop says which. media-pool-kinds cpu and media-pool-kinds models say which kinds each takes now. When a worker is stopped and no other takes its kinds, they show no worker on the Status , and the work waits until it starts again; Work that nothing will run says what to do.

These settings are in the Processing category of Settings → System , or set with config set , and come with the Media module. Saving one restarts the worker that reads it, and work in progress is picked up again. Configuration explains how. Setting Default What it decides CFG_CPU_SLOTS 2 How much work the media-worker worker runs at once. A transcode takes two slots, other kinds one. CFG_CPU_NON_ENTRY_SLOTS 1 Slots kept first for work after ingest, so a long import does not hold back thumbnails and faces. Ingest borrows them when nothing else waits. CFG_CPU_WORKERS 4 The most CPU jobs in flight; the slots are the real limit CFG_MODEL_SLOTS 2 Requests the models worker keeps in flight against the media service. Size it to what the media service runs at once. CFG_MODEL_SECOND_SLOTS 0 Requests the models-second worker keeps in flight; 0 leaves it off. Size both workers' slots together against the media service. CFG_MODEL_KIND_QUANTUM_MS 3600000 How long the models worker stays on one kind before turning to the next, so faces do not starve the rest; models-second takes a change at its next start Tip More CFG_MODEL_SLOTS than the media service runs at once only moves the wait into its queue, and past its depth into waiting for EMS . With models-second on, the media service holds two families of models at once, and both must fit on its graphics card, or one runs on the processor.

A folder can put the work on the files under it behind all other work. When its lane attribute is bulk , everything that starts for a file under it, from its reading and its renditions to the other modules' work, waits until nothing else does, so what anyone uploads meanwhile is ready first. The nearest folder above a file that sets lane decides. The Archive's staging categories set it from their lane ( Plan a large import ); on any other folder, as its owner or the administrator: # in EiN's terminal attrs -s lane=bulk /archive/imports/old-drive It applies to work announced from then on, within a minute; work already waiting keeps its place. Performance and sizing says what to set on a small or a large machine, and Change how it works , on the media service's page, how many model requests the media service admits at once, EMS_LIMIT_MODELS .

p.h: For a module's author: naming your kinds
p.x: A module names the kinds of work its pipeline steps put in the pool in drop-ins: etc/media-worker.d/kinds for the steps that take cpu , and etc/media-models.d/kinds for those that take models . mod setup links them as /etc/media-worker.d/<module>/kinds and /etc/media-models.d/<module>/kinds . A kind a line, in the order offered; reserve after a CPU kind puts it in the share kept for the work after ingest; # starts a comment: # what a file's metadata means, kept for the work after ingest interpret reserve A kind no worker takes never runs, so name every kind a step of yours declares. The workers read the drop-ins as they start, and mod install restarts them when it puts in place a module whose kinds are new or changed ( dropIns ). After you change your kinds by hand, restart them with service restart media-worker and service restart models .

p.h: For a module's author: holding a file
p.x: A module that must have its say before a file is read puts a command in etc/media-read.d/hold , which mod setup links as /etc/media-read.d/<module>/hold . Its first line that is not a comment runs before each reading as <command> <file> , with -f before the file when the reading is forced. To hold the file, the command sets hold on it: { "by" : "archive" , "reason" : "an exact copy of …" , "sha256" : "<the file's sha256>" , "within" : "<a folder>" } The hold lasts while the file has those bytes and lies under that folder. New bytes, or a move out of the folder, end it without anyone taking it off, and a forced reading reads the file anyway.

The commands the media module adds. They are there once the module is installed. 23 of them, by name. Every command also says this with --help ; Commands explains how to read an entry. compute-fingerprint · detect-chapters · embed-picture · exif-extract · file-crop · file-restore · file-set-text · file-set-text-language · file-set-transcript · find-damage · fingerprints-scan · generate-derivatives · index-document · media-bridge · media-pool-kinds · media-reembed · pictures-scan · promote-exif-attrs · read-text · regenerate · renditions-scan · text-scan · transcribe-file

Compute the fingerprints that find copies of a media file: SSCD for pictures and video keyframes, chromaprint for sound. changes things compute-fingerprint [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to media file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Force recompute even if already fingerprinted. compute-fingerprint /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the fingerprints are written under the file, and fingerprintedAt on it.

Find a video's cuts and write them as its chapters (metadata/chapters) changes things detect-chapters [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a video file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Look again even if the chapters are found. detect-chapters /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_1978/files/sommarfilm.avi With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the chapters are written as WebVTT under the file, with the cuts on the node.

Embed a photo or a video's keyframes for search by what is in the picture. changes things embed-picture [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a photo or video file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Embed again even if the model EMS runs now made the vectors. embed-picture /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the vectors written under the file's metadata/picture and the model that made them; nothing when the file's vectors are kept.

Read a media file's metadata: the probe's dump and what it says of the file under metadata/exif, and its mimetype, dimensions, angle, duration, codec and whether it can be decoded on the file. Each module's hold command runs first, and a file it holds is not read unless forced. changes things exif-extract [-f] [-v] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to file. Option What it does -f Read again even when metadata/exif already exists, and a file a module holds. -v Verbose output. exif-extract /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the exif node is written under the file and its facts on it, or nothing for a file a module holds.

Cut a part of a picture out at its own resolution, into a new file. changes things file-crop [--box=<string>] [--width=<string>] [--height=<string>] [-o <path>] <file> Argument What it is <file> The picture to cut from; it is never written. Option What it does --box=<string> x,y,width,height of the part, in fractions of the picture as it is shown (turned and flopped) --width=<string> The most pixels across the cut is written at; it is never enlarged. --height=<string> The most pixels high the cut is written at; it is never enlarged. -o <path> The file to write (--output), a .jpg, .png, .webp or .avif; it must not be there yet. file-crop /archive/scans/1952/portrait.tif --box 0.4,0.3,0.1,0.1 --width 1200 -o /tmp/eye.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : The file written, its size, and the size of the picture as shown (frame)

Restore a photo into a new version beside it: faded colours back, dust and scratches filled, blur taken out, grain lessened. changes things file-restore [--unfade] [--dust] [--dark] [--fill=<string>] [--mask=<path>] [--blur=<string>] [--grain=<string>] [--queue] [--requested] [-v] <file> Argument What it is <file> The picture to restore (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP or BMP), or with --queue any number; it is never written. Option What it does --unfade Give a faded colour print its colours back: each channel stretched, the neutral tones made grey. --dust Find dust, scratches and cracks and fill them from what surrounds them. --dark With --dust, look for damage darker than the picture too. --fill=<string> With --dust or --mask, how the damage is filled: ns (the default) or telea for dust and thin scratches, lama for creases and tears. --mask=<path> Fill what this mask marks instead of finding the damage: a one-channel PNG the size of the picture as stored, nonzero where marked. It is copied beside the version. --blur=<string> Take out blur: focus for a picture out of focus, motion for one blurred by a moving camera. --grain=<string> Lessen grain and noise, at this strength (above 0, at most 1; 0.5 keeps about half the grain) --queue Restore the pictures named in the media pool, nobody waiting: each gets its steps as restoreRequest, and a version when its turn comes. --requested Run the steps a picture's restoreRequest asks for, and clear it (what the media pool runs) -v Say each step as it runs. file-restore /archive/scans/1974/print-07.jpg --unfade --dust file-restore /archive/scans/1952/portrait.tif --dust --dark --fill lama --grain 0.5 file-restore /archive/scans/1974/print-07.jpg --unfade --mask /archive/scans/1974/print-07-mask.png file-restore /archive/scans/1968/party.jpg --blur motion file-restore --queue --unfade --dust /archive/scans/1974/*.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : The version written, with the steps that made it and, with --dust or --mask, its mask and marks; with --queue the pictures queued and those refused, and why.

Write the text in a picture by hand, in place of what was read from it. changes things file-set-text [--text=<string>] <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to a picture. Option What it does --text=<string> the text; empty removes it, - reads it from stdin. file-set-text /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/brev.jpg --text 'Kära Anna' With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the text is written and the picture is not read again.

Set the language the text in a picture is written in (or auto), and read the picture again in it. changes things file-set-text-language <file> <language> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to a picture. <language> ISO 639-1 code (sv, en, de, …), or auto to tell it from the text. file-set-text-language /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/brev.jpg en file-set-text-language /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/brev.jpg auto With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the language is set and the picture read again on the media pool.

Write what is said in a video or a recording by hand, in place of the transcript, from WebVTT on stdin. changes things file-set-transcript <file> Argument What it is <file> VFS path to a video or a recording. cat /home/admin/rattad.vtt | file-set-transcript /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the transcript is written, searchable, and not transcribed again.

Read how faded, dusty, scratched, blurred and shaken a picture is, and keep it on the file to find those worth restoring. changes things find-damage [-f] [-v] <file> Argument What it is <file> The picture to read (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP or BMP); its bytes are never written. Option What it does -f Read again even if already read. -v Say what was found, or why nothing was. find-damage /archive/scans/1974/print-07.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : The kinds of damage found (faded, dust, scratches, blurred, shaken), the scores from 0 to 1, what read them and when.

Announce every picture, video and recording that was never fingerprinted to the end: it has no fingerprintedAt. changes things fingerprints-scan [--limit=<number>] [--if-idle] [-n] [-v] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] The tree to look in (default /) Option What it does --limit=<number> Facts one run announces at most (default 1000; 0 for no cap) --if-idle Announce nothing while media-fingerprint has work waiting. -n Dry run — count what would be announced without announcing it. -v Name each file announced. fingerprints-scan -n fingerprints-scan /archive/albums/christmas-2019 fingerprints-scan --if-idle -- limit 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files it looked at and how many it announced as media.fingerprints.stale.

Generate web derivatives (still pictures, transcoded renditions, a document's PDF) for a media file or a document. changes things generate-derivatives [-v] [-f] [--only=<string>] [--size=<string>] [--prune] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to media file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Force regenerate even if derivatives exist. --only=<string> Generate one class only: still | transcode | preview | storyboard. --size=<string> Generate only these roles (comma-separated): roles of /etc/renditions.yaml, storyboard, or pdf. --prune Delete renditions under thumbnails/ that are no longer targets. generate-derivatives /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg generate-derivatives --only still /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; the thumbnail, display and transcode renditions are written, and the file is marked (renditionsFor, renditionsAt) once it has every one the table owes it.

Extract text content and generate embedding for a document file. changes things index-document [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to document file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Force reindex even if already indexed.

Derive the facts of a media file itself from VFS mutations: arrived, changed, turned, removed, read, its renditions made, its text and transcript, and the unread files a moved directory carried (long-running) changes things media-bridge media-bridge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; it runs until stopped, turning VFS mutations into the facts of media files.

The kinds of work a worker of the media pool takes, from the modules' drop-ins, as pipeline-worker's flags. reads only media-pool-kinds [--reverse] [--instance=<string>] [--expect=<string>] <worker> Argument What it is <worker> cpu (the media-worker service) or models (models and models-second) Option What it does --reverse The kinds in the reverse order, as the second models worker takes them. --instance=<string> The kinds for a worker of this EMS instance: those it serves every op of and stamps as the primary does (main, the primary, takes every kind) --expect=<string> Print nothing, and exit 1 unless the flags would be these. media-pool-kinds cpu media-pool-kinds models --reverse media-pool-kinds models --instance laptop JSON_OUTPUT=1 media-pool-kinds models With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the flags (--kind for each kind, --reserve-kind for each reserved one); in JSON the kinds in order and the reserved ones.

Embed the extracted texts, transcripts and hand-written descriptions already stored into the current text space, from the stored text alone. changes things media-reembed [-l <number>] [-f] [-v] [<path>...] Argument What it is [<path>...] files to embed the texts of (default: every text the archive holds) Option What it does -l <number> stop after this many texts or transcripts (default: all); a run resumes where the last stopped. -f embed again even what the current embedder already made. -v name each transcript as it is done. media-reembed media-reembed -l 5000 media-reembed /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0001.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many texts, transcripts and descriptions were embedded, skipped and failed; pass complete once nothing is left.

Announce every photo and video whose picture vectors are not the model EMS embeds with now: its marker is missing or names another model. changes things pictures-scan [--limit=<number>] [--if-idle] [-n] [-v] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] The tree to look in (default /) Option What it does --limit=<number> Facts one run announces at most (default 1000; 0 for no cap) --if-idle Announce nothing while media-embed-picture has work waiting. -n Dry run — count what would be announced without announcing it. -v Name each file announced. pictures-scan -n pictures-scan /archive/albums/christmas-2019 pictures-scan --if-idle -- limit 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files it looked at and how many it announced as media.picture.stale, and the model EMS embeds with.

Copy width/height/duration from a file's exif node onto the file node. changes things promote-exif-attrs [-v] [-n] [--angle] [--codec] <path> Argument What it is <path> VFS path to a media file or a directory to walk. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -n Dry run — report what would be set, write nothing. --angle Also promote a video's container rotation to angle (never a still's, never over angleManual) --codec Also promote a video's picture codec to codec (the hint EMS skips its VRAM stage on) promote-exif-attrs /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/IMG_0007.jpg With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : nothing; width, height and duration are copied from the exif node onto the file.

Read the text written in a picture and keep it for search. changes things read-text [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to a picture. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Read again even if already read.

Regenerate web derivatives for media files under a path. changes things regenerate [--force] [--prune] [--size=<string>] [--mime=<string>] [--verbose] <target> Argument What it is <target> VFS path to file or directory. Option What it does --force , -f Force regenerate even if derivatives exist. --prune Delete renditions that are no longer part of the target set. --size=<string> , -s Generate only these roles, comma-separated: roles of /etc/renditions.yaml, or storyboard (e.g. small,medium) --mime=<string> Only files whose mimetype matches this glob (e.g. 'video/*') --verbose , -v Verbose output. regenerate /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019 regenerate --force --size thumb /archive/albums With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files had their derivatives regenerated.

Announce every file whose renditions are not those the rendition table names now: its marker is missing or names another table, or a rendition was refused under a CPU budget EMS no longer runs. changes things renditions-scan [--limit=<number>] [--if-idle] [-n] [-v] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] The tree to look in (default /) Option What it does --limit=<number> Facts one run announces at most (default 1000; 0 for no cap) --if-idle Announce nothing while the rendition pipelines have work waiting. -n Dry run — count what would be announced without announcing it. -v Name each file announced. renditions-scan -n renditions-scan /archive/recipes renditions-scan --if-idle -- limit 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files it looked at and how many it announced as media.renditions.stale.

Announce every file whose text, transcript or text vectors are missing or not what EMS makes now, found by their markers. changes things text-scan [--limit=<number>] [--if-idle] [-n] [-v] [<path>] Argument What it is [<path>] The tree to look in (default /) Option What it does --limit=<number> Facts one run announces at most (default 1000; 0 for no cap) --if-idle Hold back each fact whose pipeline has work waiting. -n Dry run — count what would be announced without announcing it. -v Name each file announced. text-scan -n text-scan /archive/albums/christmas-2019 text-scan --if-idle -- limit 0 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : how many files it looked at and how many it announced, by fact, and the facts it held back or could not check.

Transcribe audio or video into a timed WebVTT node with chunk embeddings. changes things transcribe-file [-v] [-f] <input> Argument What it is <input> VFS path to an audio or video file. Option What it does -v Verbose output. -f Transcribe again even a transcript made with the settings EMS runs now, unless it was written by hand. transcribe-file /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/files/MVI_0042.MOV With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the transcript written, or the one kept; a timed WebVTT transcript with chunk embeddings is written under the file.

The media service, EMS, holds every media tool and model the Archive uses: it reads metadata, makes thumbnails and video renditions, finds faces, voices and text, transcribes speech and makes pictures searchable. This section applies once the Archive is installed, and this page is for the administrator who installs the media service, watches it and tunes it.

The media service comes in two parts, installed in different ways: The ems module , EiN's side of it: the client the Archive calls the media service through, its health on the Status , with the Media service tab and the graphics card's readings, and ems-text-embed , which turns text into vectors so that things can be found by meaning. Installing the archive module installs the ems module with it ( Modules ). The media service itself , the ems container that runs beside EiN. The installer's --ems adds it ( Add the media service ); the module does not. The Archive needs both: without them, nothing it takes in gets thumbnails, dates, faces or searchable text. Without the Archive they have nothing to do. The one other use of them is the assistant's command search, which with their text vectors finds commands by meaning ( Find the command you need ).

EiN itself runs no media tool. Whenever a file needs looking at, EiN sends the media service a request naming the file, and the media service answers or writes the result where EiN asked. It keeps no data of its own and knows nothing of the tree: it reads the files EiN stores, and nothing else. Work What you see in EiN Reading dates, places, cameras and codecs Dates and places on pictures; staging can group files Thumbnails, picture sizes, posters and waveforms Pictures, videos and recordings show in the grids and the viewer Video and audio renditions (AV1 video, AAC audio) Videos and recordings play in the browser Faces, voices and who is speaking People and faces Transcripts and language detection What is said in videos and recordings, searchable Text in pictures and handwriting, text in documents Text found in photographed pages, letters and PDFs, searchable Picture and text vectors Finding pictures by what they show, and text by meaning Fingerprints and copy detection Duplicates Shot boundaries Chapters in a video The media service generates no text. The chat belongs to the assistant's language model , and no processing step depends on it.

With the Archive installed and no media service, EiN still takes in, keeps and shares what you upload, but nothing new is read: Uploads wait in staging as being prepared . New files get no metadata, thumbnails, faces, transcripts or search vectors. The Status shows the warning http://ems:8181 is not answering; work that needs it waits on its Overview tab. A warning does not stop Healthy . None of this work is lost. Each step that needs the media service waits without using up its retries, and runs once the media service answers again.

The media service's own code is under the MIT licence, as The licence explains. The media service's image also downloads and carries models and tools made by others, each under its own licence. None of their own licences forbids commercial use; two state no licence for their weights, and GFPGAN's names parts under non-commercial terms ( Using EiN commercially ). — means the media service runs the weights with no code of the model's own, through the libraries the models run on. These are under permissive licences: PyTorch under a BSD-style licence , ONNX Runtime and CTranslate2 under MIT , and transformers , sentence-transformers and OpenCV under Apache-2.0 . The image passes each model's weights on unmodified: as their maker publishes them or, where the table names an export or a conversion, as the one who made it publishes it. They come as is, without warranties, as their licences say. Beside them, the image writes out two files derived from published ones: the Finnish handwriting recogniser's character list, and TrOCR's tokenizer in the format transformers reads. The image's /usr/share/doc/ein-ems/NOTICE.md points to this page, names the models under Creative Commons, Apache-2.0 and MIT, links the Creative Commons licences and holds the texts of Apache-2.0 and MIT. None of EMS's own tools is under the GPL: it encodes AV1 only, so its FFmpeg and its HEIC reader are builds without the GPL encoders x264 and x265. The image carries one FFmpeg, which also fingerprints recordings with the Chromaprint built into it, and faster-whisper is installed without PyAV, since the media service hands it audio FFmpeg has already decoded. The image's GPL code is Debian's, programs such as bash and coreutils among its packages. NOTICE.md names FFmpeg's build and where the source of it and of Debian's packages is.

The media service's own code is under the MIT licence, which allows any use, commercial use included. EiN may be used commercially too, but offering it to others as a hosted service needs a licence from its author, since its core is under the Elastic License: The licence says what is allowed. No model or tool in the table is under terms that forbid commercial use. Two models' weights state no licence of their own: Microsoft's TrOCR large handwritten, which reads English handwriting, and Meta's SSCD, which finds copies of pictures and videos, whose code is under MIT. An installation used commercially checks those two with their makers. GFPGAN, which redraws faces in scanned photos when someone asks for it, is under Apache-2.0, but its LICENSE also lists StyleGAN2 (NVIDIA's Source Code License, for non-commercial use) and DFDNet (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) among its third-party parts, without saying which files they are; the media service runs its clean network, which uses none of StyleGAN2's CUDA code. Its weights state no licence of their own and were trained on FFHQ, a dataset NVIDIA releases under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. An installation used commercially checks GFPGAN with its makers too, or leaves face restoration out. Restormer, which sharpens a scanned photo out of focus or shaken when someone asks for it, and its weights are under MIT. Its weights for photos out of focus were trained on DPDD, a dataset of photographs whose licence is stated nowhere; those for a shaken camera on GoPro, under CC BY 4.0. The licences in the table set conditions on passing a model or tool on: CC BY 4.0 a credit to its maker and a link to the licence, Apache-2.0 a copy of the licence and MIT its copyright notice, which this page and the image's notice give; GPL and LGPL conditions on passing the software and its source on. Check each licence for what it asks of your installation.

The installer adds it with --ems , at the first install or any time after: On the machine EiN runs on, run: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein ./setup.sh --ems With the Archive not installed yet, add it in the same run: ./setup.sh --ems --module archive installs the media service, and the Archive with the ems module at EiN's start. Wait for the download. The first time, setup.sh prints == Getting the images (the media service the first time: about 30 GB) : the image carries every model, and downloading it takes a while and about 30 GB of disk. Installed from your own source, it is built on the machine instead, which takes about an hour more. Install EiN lists what the machine needs with the media service. setup.sh starts the containers and prints EiN is up at http://…:8080/ once EiN answers. Open Status under System in the sidebar, and choose the Media service tab. For the first minutes the media service loads its models; the tab then shows the healthy badge. --ems writes EIN_EMS=1 to ~/ein/.env , so a later ./setup.sh keeps it. When setup.sh found an NVIDIA card with its CDI spec at the first install ( EIN_GPU=1 ), the media service gets the card; The graphics card explains how. To leave the media service out again, run ./setup.sh --no-ems . Its container stops and is removed; your files and everything already made from them stay.

In the standard install, both containers run on the same machine and only EiN talks to the media service, on the compose network. Nothing outside the machine reaches it. Three things connect them, all set up by setup.sh : What Where it is set Value The address CFG_EMS_URL for EiN, in compose.yaml http://ems:8181 The key EMS_KEY in .env , made at the install; EiN gets it as CFG_EMS_KEY 48 random hexadecimal characters The files' way CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS for EiN, which setup.sh writes ein:2224 , or host.containers.internal:2224 ; see below The key is a secret: no shell in EiN sees it, and the settings page never shows it once it is set. The media service accepts a request only with that key. Leave CFG_EMS_URL , EMS_KEY and EMS_PORT as setup.sh and the compose files set them; Configuration explains how a value set in the deployment relates to the settings page.

A program on another machine of your network can use the media service too, such as a scanning station that sends it photos to restore. Two lines make that possible: # in ~/ein/.env EIN_EMS_BIND = 192.168 . 1.20 # in ~/ein/ems.keys, a line a caller: its key, its name and its weight 4f6c…e1 scanner 1 EIN_EMS_BIND publishes the media service on that address of this machine, or on every address with 0.0.0.0 , at EIN_EMS_PORT (18181). It answers plain HTTP with no certificate, so publish it only on a network you trust. ems.keys gives each caller a key of its own; the weight is its share of the media service when requests wait, so a caller with a long queue does not hold EiN up, which keeps EMS_KEY as the caller default . setup.sh mounts the file into the media service when it is there. Run ./setup.sh after changing either. The caller names the media service http://<this machine>:18181 and serves its own files the way EiN does ( How the media service reaches your files ).

p.h: How the media service reaches your files
p.x: The media service mounts none of EiN's folders. It reaches the files of each request through EiN's ems-files service, on the port CFG_EMS_FILES_PORT (2224), at the address CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS names: EiN's name on the compose network, or, when EiN has a network of its own under rootless podman, the machine's own address, where setup.sh publishes the port. Every request EiN sends names it, and the media service mounts it with sshfs, reads the request's files through the mount, and writes what it made back through it before it answers: Each request has a folder of its own there, and each file in it a name of its own: a number and the file's name in EiN, such as 0-IMG_0001.JPG . The media service never sees where a file is in EiN or on the disk. Only the files of requests in flight are there, each only while its request runs: the files it reads, read-only, and the files it writes, write-only. Nothing can be listed, removed or renamed, and your originals can never be changed. A tool reads only the part of a file it needs, as it would on a folder of its own, and what was read stays cached for the next step on the same file until the file changes. The connection carries the files and nothing else. Before it does, the media service proves it is the one EiN is sending requests to: ems-files sends a random challenge, which it answers with a secret made when ems-files starts and sent along with each request. Nothing is configured on the media service's side, and a restart leaves no secret behind that still works. By default the connection is not encrypted, which costs half the processor time and suits the standard install, where both run on the same machine and nothing else is on the compose network. The requests to the media service are not encrypted there either. The media service's container has /dev/fuse and the SYS_ADMIN capability for the mount, which setup.sh gives it. Without a mount it refuses the request, and the step that sent it waits and tries again, as when the media service is away. While CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS is empty, EiN sends no request that names a file, and those steps wait the same way. A media service on another machine reaches EiN's machine at the address you set: put CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS , as host:port , in ~/ein/.env and run ./setup.sh , which then publishes the port on EIN_BIND . A second media service beside the first reaches it at an address of its own ( More than one media service ). Encrypting the files' way When the media service reaches EiN over a network you do not trust, turn on CFG_EMS_FILES_TLS . Each connection is then TLS: ems-files and the media service each have a certificate made when ems-files starts, each accepts only the other's, and both reach the media service with each request, so there is still nothing to set up on its side. It costs about twice the processor time of the default. Set it on the settings page or in the deployment as any other setting; ems-files restarts with it. The certificates, and the key the media service proves itself with, travel in the requests EiN sends it, so they are only as private as those requests are. Over a network you do not trust, put the media service behind an HTTPS proxy too and give its https:// address as CFG_EMS_URL ; otherwise anyone who can read the requests can read the key with them. Faster reading through the mount The kernel reads ahead only 128 KiB on an sshfs mount, so a big video comes through at a fraction of what the network carries. On the machine the media service runs on, a rule for udev raises it to 4 MiB for every new mount, a moment after the mount, which is when the setting holds: # on the machine the media service runs on echo 'ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="bdi", KERNEL=="0:*", RUN+="/bin/sh -c ' \' 'sleep 1; echo 4096 > /sys/class/bdi/%k/read_ahead_kb' \' '"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/90-fuse-readahead.rules sudo udevadm control --reload The rule takes effect at the media service's next mount, which it makes again whenever EiN restarts. cat /sys/class/bdi/0:*/read_ahead_kb shows 4096 for a mount made after it. On the test machine one video read at 145 MB/s with it, against 20 MB/s without.

Open Status under System and choose the Media service tab. It asks the media service how it is, again and again, while the tab is open. With no indexing work the card is quiet: search runs on it, and a copy in RAM stands by for when indexing takes it. Media service : a badge, healthy , degraded or model worker down , and the facts: version , commit , api , uptime , batch worker and query worker ( up , or down , with × and the number of restarts), card , driver and url . Under them, when there is a card, Graphics card says who has it now, since when, and when that changes (see The graphics card below). An orange box for each degradation, such as gpu degraded , and a yellow one for each warning. Where the models are : two bars. Graphics card splits the card's memory into each model on it, the media service's own runtime there, the chat model and others that share the card, and what is free. RAM splits the media service's memory into each model held there and its workers' own. A search model drawn hatched, as standby , is in RAM as well as on the card while the card is quiet: the card answers the searches, and the RAM copy answers the moment indexing takes the card, so search never stops. Under the card's bar, Media service's share sets how much of the card the media service may hold ( Share one card with the language model ). Under the bars, the RAM each worker rebuilds itself at, and how many times it has. How busy the card is, its temperature and its power are the GPU tile of the Media service card on the Overview tab. Models : every model the media service can load, in four columns by what it is doing, Working , Loaded, idle , Loading or unloading and Not loaded , each with where it is and its size. Hover a model's name for what it does. Every model in detail opens the full table: where each runs when indexing has the card and when it is quiet, its size, and when it was loaded and last used. The last 6 hours : a row for each model that was loaded, solid where it was on the card, outlined where it was in RAM and underlined while it worked, under the card's mode and the work EiN had waiting. A model loaded again and again shows as a row that flickers. The ems-sampler service records what the media service holds once a minute, for a week. Executing : the requests running or waiting now, and the four lanes they go through, models , tools , encodes and watches (a camera's frames on their way to the faces model, when a camera is watched for faces ), each with how many run at once. When requests wait, a request a person is waiting on goes first. Then, when more than one system sends the media service work, the system that has used it the least; the tab then shows Callers too, each system with how much it has used and what it runs and waits for now. Of that system's requests, one for a model that is already working goes first, so the media service does not load one model after another, unless another has waited five minutes. When the media service does not answer, the tab shows only The media service is not answering , with the address it tried. The Work tab's Where the work is ends with the media service's part: At the media service , its four lanes with their slots and the requests in them, and On a model , the models it holds, the working ones first and the search models apart. With more than one media service , the tab lists them beside it, and the Work tab's two columns have a group for each. The Overview tab shows the machine the media service runs on as the Media service card, beside the card of the machine EiN runs on, even when they are the same machine: its CPU, its memory and, when it has a graphics card, the card's use and memory. With no card the GPU tiles are not there, and with no media service the card is not there until it first answers. The media service's machine as a device The machine the media service runs on is a device too, /dev/ems , of class host , under Devices , beside the one for the machine EiN runs on ( Core's host driver ). It is a device of its own even when both run on one machine. Another instance is /dev/ems-<name> ( More than one media service ). The ems-sampler service makes it on the media service's first answer and writes its readings every 15 seconds through the ems driver; the device is online while the media service answers, so a rule can act when it goes away. Only the administrators see it. Endpoint Reading Kept gpu How busy the card is, in % 30 days decoder , encoder How busy the card's video decoder and encoder are, in % 30 days vram-used The share of the card's memory in use, in % 30 days gpu-temperature The card's temperature, in °C 30 days gpu-power What the card draws, in W 30 days memory-used The share of the machine's memory in use, in % 30 days cpu , load The share of the machine's processor cores in use, in %, and its 1-minute load 30 days vram-total , memory-total The card's and the machine's memory, in GB 365 days gpu-power-limit The most the card may draw, in W 365 days The card's readings are there only when the media service sees a card, and cpu and load only from a media service of API 0.3.4 or later. The Media service card on the System status page's Overview draws them, and ems-gpu and ems-memory read them back in the terminal, ems-memory with the media service's own share of the memory. What the media service holds and does, its models, lanes and requests, is not the machine's and stays on the Media service tab. The Media service card is the media service's machine; its GPU and VRAM tiles show only when it has a card About EiN in the account menu also has a Media service tile: its version, the API it speaks, its commit, how long it has been up and the card it runs on, or Not answering .

The Status page's verdict and the health command read these checks about the media service: Check State When ems ok It answers: EMS <commit> answering, up <time> ems warn It does not answer: <address> is not answering; work that needs it waits ems worker warn the model worker is down; EMS starts it again ems gpu fail The card is meant to be there and is not, or the card stopped working ems card ok Who has the card, busy or quiet , and which search models are on it Only ems gpu fails, and a failed check turns the verdict to Needs a person . The others are warnings: while the media service restarts or loads its models, the work that needs it waits. Each other instance has the same checks under its name, ems laptop and so on.

ems-status prints the whole answer the Status page draws, and its options shorten it: # in EiN's terminal ems-status # everything: version, models, requests, card, memory ems-status --brief # one line, degradations first ems-status --checks # the checks above ems-gpu # the card now, with the last six hours ok ems EMS 3f9a2c1 answering, up 2.4h ok ems card quiet, search on it: text-query, siglip-text service-list --detail shows the same one line as ems-status --brief beside the ems-link service. When the media service does not answer, ems-status says ems-status: http://ems:8181 is not answering and exits with 1.

The media service is the ems service of compose: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose ps ems # or docker compose podman compose logs -f ems # what it says, as it says it podman compose restart ems Compose checks it every 30 seconds, and gives it 120 seconds to start before a failed check counts.

The media service uses an NVIDIA card when it has one, and the CPU otherwise. Without a card every model and every encoder still runs, only more slowly. Where each model runs is the media service's own decision, made each time it loads one; it changes how fast an answer comes, never what it is. A model that does not fit on the card runs on the CPU, except transcription and the Swedish and Finnish handwriting reader, which wait for room on the card. To make room, the media service unloads the models used longest ago first, and only as many as it needs. With a card, the media service hands the card between indexing and search, and Graphics card mode on the Media service tab shows which has it: Mode What it means busy Indexing has the graphics card and search runs on the CPU, until no indexing work has come for a while. quiet No indexing work, so its models are unloaded and search runs on the graphics card, as far as it fits. switching Handing the graphics card over between indexing and search. off No graphics card to share: every model runs where its setting says. When the mode is off, which EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER=0 makes it too, the tab leaves Graphics card out. It turns quiet after 600 seconds without indexing work ( EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER ). A search never waits for the card: a separate model process answers searches on the CPU throughout. The graphics card covers preparing the machine, checking that every model really runs on the card, sharing the card with the language model and being told when the card goes missing .

The media service is configured by its environment alone. ~/ein/.env is that environment, so an EMS_ line there reaches it: Add or change the line in ~/ein/.env : # in ~/ein/.env EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGES =sv,en Apply it: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose up -d Under podman-compose, a container that podman compose up -d makes again has no swap limit, so the media service's idle models may go to swap and a search waits for them; ./setup.sh makes the containers again with the limit. Any change restarts the media service, and EiN with it, since both read .env . Requests in flight fail and are retried; see When the media service restarts . These are the settings an administrator is most likely to need: Setting Default What it does EMS_MEMORY 16g The most memory the container may use. Compose reads it, not the media service. EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGES empty The languages spoken in your recordings, as codes separated by commas, the most common first. Detection is biased towards them; empty lets detection alone decide. EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGE empty One language every recording is transcribed as; detection never runs. Right only when every recording is in that language. EMS_EXPECT_GPU empty 1 : the machine is meant to have a card, and the ems gpu check fails when none is visible. EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB empty The most of the card the media service holds when it starts, in MB, until EiN's CFG_EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB gives it another; empty is all of it, 0 none. Share one card . EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER 600 Seconds without indexing work before search gets the card; 0 keeps search on the CPU. EMS_MODEL_IDLE_EVICT 21600 Seconds a model may sit unused before it is unloaded. EMS_MODEL_PINNED text-query Models loaded at start and never unloaded, separated by commas. The search models, text-query and siglip-text , are pinned in the query worker whatever this says, and only there, so the default pins nothing unless EMS_QUERY_WORKER=0 . EMS_MODEL_MAX_RSS 0.6 of the container's memory The batch worker's memory ceiling, such as 10g . At the ceiling the worker finishes its requests and starts again; 0 turns the ceiling off. EMS_LIMIT_MODELS 8 Model requests admitted at once. EMS_LIMIT_TOOLS 4 Tool requests at once: metadata, thumbnails, fingerprints, document text. Each tool uses one core, so this is a number of cores. EMS_LIMIT_ENCODES 2 Transcodes and other whole-file decodes at once. EMS_QUEUE_DEPTH 64 Requests of one system that may wait before a new one of its own is answered busy . EMS_WATCHES 4 Cameras watched for faces at once: each holds a decode of its stream, and asks for faces a few times a second while it moves. EMS_AFFINITY_WAIT 300 Seconds a model request may wait while requests for a model already working go before it. EMS_INTERACTIVE_RESERVE 1 Slots more for a request a person is waiting on, so a person never waits behind indexing. EMS_VIDEO_ENCODER empty The video encoder: empty picks av1_nvenc on a card that offers it and libsvtav1 otherwise. EMS_CPU_ENCODE_MAX_MB 4000 Memory one video decode on the CPU may grow to. A long video is encoded in pieces within it; one that cannot be is refused. 0 turns the CPU encode off. EMS_TOOL_STALL 900 Seconds a tool may go without using the CPU or moving a byte before it is stopped as stuck. Not a limit on how long it may take. Warning Leave EMS_WHISPER_MODEL as it is ( large-v3 ). It must match the model built into the image; another name makes the first transcription download one, or fail without a network. A change to the transcription settings changes what EMS reports as its transcript settings. With Keep transcripts current ( CFG_MEDIA_TRANSCRIPTS_CURRENT ) left on, the Media module then transcribes every video and recording again in the background, behind new media ( Text and transcripts kept current ). On a large archive that is hours of work.

EiN's own settings for the media service are in the Media service and Transcription groups of Settings → System , with CFG_MODEL_SLOTS , the Media module's, in Processing . All can be set with config set : Setting Default What it does CFG_EMS_URL http://127.0.0.1:8181 ; the install sets http://ems:8181 Where the media service answers CFG_EMS_KEY none; the install sets it The key the media service expects CFG_EMS_CONNECT_RETRY 90 Seconds a background request keeps retrying while the media service refuses connections CFG_EMS_LINK_INTERVAL_SECONDS 60 How often ems-link asks whether the media service answers CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS empty; the install sets it Where the media service reaches EiN's files; empty: steps that name a file wait CFG_EMS_FILES_PORT 2224 The port ems-files listens on while that address is set CFG_EMS_FILES_TLS false Encrypt the media service's file connections with TLS CFG_WHISPER_LANGUAGE empty A language sent with every transcription; empty lets the media service decide CFG_WHISPER_VAD_MIN_SILENCE_MS empty The pause that ends a stretch of speech CFG_WHISPER_WORD_TIMESTAMPS empty 1 for the time of every word, 0 for timings per segment CFG_MODEL_SLOTS 2 Model requests the models worker keeps in flight against the media service at once For the languages of a family archive, prefer EMS_WHISPER_LANGUAGES in .env to CFG_WHISPER_LANGUAGE : the first biases detection, so a holiday clip in English is still transcribed as English; the second forces one language on everything. Media explains CFG_MODEL_SLOTS and the other slots.

A restart takes tens of seconds, longer when models load. Meanwhile: A background request that finds the connection refused tries again for up to CFG_EMS_CONNECT_RETRY seconds (90) before the step gives up for now. A step that cannot reach the media service, finds it busy , or finds a model still loading waits without using up an attempt, and runs again later. A request a person is waiting on, such as a search, does not wait: it fails at once. The ems-link service writes each change to its log, such as ems-link: down — not answering and ems-link: up — … . When the media service comes back with a different build, ems-link runs every failed pipeline instance again at once, since a new build is the likeliest fix for what failed under the old one. It logs ems-link: EMS <old> -> <new>; failed work runs again: … . Services and logs shows how to read that log.

./setup.sh without options downloads the newest images of EiN and of each service it runs, the media service included, and starts them again. Only the layers that changed are downloaded. Updating has the whole procedure.

The Media service tab says The media service is not answering. Look at the container: podman compose ps ems . If it is not running, podman compose logs ems says why; start it with podman compose up -d . If .env has EIN_EMS=0 , the media service is not installed: run ./setup.sh --ems . It answers, but the badge says model worker down. The model process stopped; the media service starts it again by itself. If it keeps stopping, the count after × beside batch worker climbs: podman compose logs ems says why. When it ran out of memory, give the container more with EMS_MEMORY in .env . Work waits for the media service although it answers and runs nothing. health says … waiting for EMS, which could not run it yet again and again, while the Media service tab shows no request executing. What the media service answered the last step that could not run ends the kind's line in health , after it said: or the last could not run … ago: , and on the Status page it follows the line that is not moving; the whole error is on each waiting step ( JSON_OUTPUT=1 pipeline-status <id> , its error ). When it ends sshfs: fuse: mount failed: Permission denied (files_unavailable) , the media service cannot mount the files of its requests. Under Docker on Ubuntu and Debian, the container's AppArmor profile denies the mount. compose.ems.yaml turns it off for the media service; ./setup.sh brings the install's copy of that file up to date. Then pool-wake in EiN's terminal starts the waiting work at once. gpu degraded and the verdict is Needs a person. The card the machine should have is not visible to the media service, or its context was lost. A reboot that renumbers the cards is the usual cause; The graphics card has the fix. A warning no keys configured: authentication is off . The media service got no key. Check that EMS_KEY is in ~/ein/.env , and run podman compose up -d . A warning no roots configured: every file request will be refused . EMS_ROOTS is empty. It is set in compose.ems.yaml ; undo a change to that file with git -C ~/ein checkout compose.ems.yaml and run podman compose up -d . Uploads stay being prepared for a long time. Look at Executing on the Media service tab. Requests waiting in the lanes mean the media service is busy: after a large import, the Status reads Catching up until the work is done. With a card, a model shown as CPU loaded is several times slower than on the card; see Performance and sizing . The first transcription or face search after a quiet spell is slow. Models are unloaded after EMS_MODEL_IDLE_EVICT seconds unused, and loading one again takes tens of seconds. The Models table shows it as loading. The download or the build fails, or the disk fills. The media service's image is about 30 GB, and podman downloads or builds it in a folder beside its own storage, not in /tmp . Free space there and run ./setup.sh again. Troubleshooting covers problems that are not the media service's own.
