This page is for whoever runs the media service or the assistant's language model on their own machine and wants them to use an NVIDIA graphics card: what the card speeds up, what the machine needs before EiN can reach it, how EiN is given the card, how to check that it uses it, and how the two share one card. It applies once the media service or the Assistant 's own language model is installed: it is the media service's page for the card, and also the one for the language model's use of it. Nothing in EiN needs a card; without one everything runs on the processor, more slowly.

p.h: What the card is used for
p.x: Two of EiN's optional services use the card. EiN itself and its database never do. Service What runs on the card The media service ( ems , the --ems option) The models for faces, voices, transcripts, text in pictures and handwriting, picture and text vectors; AV1 video encoding The language model ( llm , the --llm option) As many of the model's layers as fit in the part of the card left to it A card changes how fast the work is done, not what comes out of it, with one exception. Each model family is placed when the media service loads it: on the card when there is room, otherwise on the processor with the same weights. Transcripts are the exception: on a machine with a card, whisper always runs on the card and a transcription waits for room there rather than move to the processor; on a machine without one it runs on the processor, at about twice the length of the recording. The two give slightly different words, so a transcript never depends on what else happened to be on the card. The handwriting readers also wait for room on the card rather than move, since on the processor they are ten to seventy times slower and a page there held up the rest of the indexing. The English one, needed far less often, unloads the Swedish and Finnish one only when no other model gives it room. The Swedish and Finnish one stays on the card for as long as the text reader is working, though only some pages need it: a model coming onto the card beside it, the faces' or the pictures' search model, runs on the processor for a minute or so until another has been idle long enough to give its room, rather than unload a reader that takes a minute or more to load again. Card Transcripts Everything else Language model 16 GB on the card on the card on the card 12 GB on the card on the card when there is room, or the processor partly on the card 8 GB on the card on the card when there is room, or the processor on the processor none on the processor, about 2x the recording on the processor on the processor A smaller card only makes the work slower: every output is made on any card or none. Video renditions are AV1. The media service encodes them on the card when the card and its build offer the av1_nvenc encoder, and on the processor otherwise; on a card without an AV1 encoder the attempt on the card fails and the processor encodes the video instead. EMS_VIDEO_ENCODER=libsvtav1 in ~/ein/.env keeps video encoding on the processor. Search uses the card too, when the media service has no indexing work: after 10 minutes without any, it unloads its indexing models and moves the search models onto the card, as far as they fit, and gives the card back to indexing as soon as work arrives. The Media service tab on the Status page shows which of the two has it, under Check that EiN uses the card .

NVIDIA only. EiN uses no other make of card. Driver 610 or newer. The media service's ffmpeg needs it to encode video on the card. 16 GB of card memory is recommended : room for the media models and the language model side by side. Cards of 8 and 12 GB work, as the table above shows. A transcription needs about 4 GB of the card free. One card. When the machine has several, EiN hands all of them to both services; it is built and tried with one. The installer checks the card when you install with --ems or --llm . It reports the card with the most memory, and every graphics line is at most low , never missing : without a usable card the install goes on and the services run on the processor. graphics ok NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070, 12282 MB, driver 610.31 card memory low 12282 MB: works; 16 GB is recommended, room for the media models and the assistant side by side container GPU ok nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.1, CDI spec in /var/run/cdi To run only the checks, without installing anything: # on the machine that will run EiN curl -fsSL https://einhq.eu/install.sh | bash -s -- --check --ems --llm

The containers reach the card through CDI, the Container Device Interface: a file that describes the card's devices and libraries, which the container engine reads when a container asks for nvidia.com/gpu=all . These steps need root, once per machine and again after reinstalling its operating system. Install NVIDIA's driver, 610 or newer, from your distribution or from NVIDIA. Check it: # on the machine EiN runs on nvidia-smi It lists the card, its memory and the driver version. When it says it cannot reach the driver, fix that first: nothing below works without it. Install nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18 or newer, from NVIDIA's package repository. 1.18 is the first that ships nvidia-cdi-refresh.service , which writes the CDI file /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml from the devices the machine actually has, at every boot and whenever the driver or the toolkit changes. Check the version: # on the machine EiN runs on nvidia-ctk --version Turn the refresh on, and check that it wrote the file: # on the machine EiN runs on sudo systemctl enable --now nvidia-cdi-refresh.service ls -l /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml Remove any CDI file made by hand. Do not run nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/… yourself: such a file names the card numbers of the moment it was made, and podman falls back to it after a reboot has renumbered them. The installer warns about it with with a hand-made spec in /etc/cdi . Check your container engine: Engine What it needs podman podman 5 reads the CDI file as it is. Versions before 5, such as 4.9.3 in Ubuntu 24.04 and Linux Mint 22, need the fix in the next section. Docker Docker Engine 28.2 or newer, where CDI is on by default. The installer checks both, and reports a podman before 5 that would reject the file, or a Docker before 28.2, as low on its container GPU line. Check that a container sees the card: # on the machine EiN runs on, as the user EiN runs as podman run -- rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all docker.io/library/debian:trixie-slim nvidia-smi -L With Docker, write docker run --rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all instead. It prints one line per card. When it fails with unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all , the engine cannot read the CDI file: see the next section.

p.h: Fix the CDI file for podman before 5
p.x: podman before 5, such as 4.9.3, rejects the CDI file as nvidia-ctk 1.17 and newer writes it, with unknown field "additionalGids" , and a container asking for nvidia.com/gpu=all then finds no card. The media service's repository has a script that makes every regeneration of the file readable to it, once per machine: Make sure the machine has Python's YAML library, which the fix uses. On Ubuntu and Mint: # on the machine EiN runs on sudo apt install python3-yaml Run the installer for the fix. After an install with --ems , the media service's sources are in ~/ein/src/ems : # on the machine EiN runs on sudo bash ~/ein/src/ems/deploy/install-cdi-refresh.sh Without the media service, fetch its repository first with git clone https://github.com/einhq/ems.git and run deploy/install-cdi-refresh.sh from there. The script copies the fix to /usr/local/sbin/ems-fix-cdi , adds it to nvidia-cdi-refresh.service as a step that runs after every regeneration, removes /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml if there is one, and regenerates the file at once. It ends with the service's status and a count of the cdiVersion , additionalGids and /dev/dri/card lines in /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml : after the fix, cdiVersion: 0.6.0 and no additionalGids . It keeps working across reboots and toolkit upgrades, and running it again does no harm. Then try the check in step 6 again.

The first setup.sh , the one the installer runs, looks for a card. When nvidia-smi works and a CDI file exists in /var/run/cdi or /etc/cdi , it writes EIN_GPU=1 into ~/ein/.env ; otherwise EIN_GPU=0 . From then on, every run of setup.sh gives the card to the media service and the language model, whichever of them you installed, by writing it into ~/ein/compose.override.yaml . Under podman, with both installed, the file reads: # Written by setup.sh from the options in .env and the container engine; edit those and run # setup.sh again. services: db: restart: always ein: environment: CFG_LLM_CARD: card restart: always ems: extends: { file: compose.ems.yaml , service: ems } devices: [ nvidia.com/gpu=all ] restart: always llm: extends: { file: compose.llm.yaml , service: llm } devices: [ nvidia.com/gpu=all ] restart: always Under Docker the restart: always lines are left out. CFG_LLM_CARD tells EiN where its own language model runs, card or cpu , so the chat and the health checks can say so ( setting ). setup.sh looks for the card only when it first writes .env . When you add a card, or prepare the machine, after EiN is installed, turn it on yourself: Open ~/ein/.env and set: # in ~/ein/.env EIN_GPU = 1 Run setup.sh , which writes compose.override.yaml again and starts the services with the card: # on the machine EiN runs on ~/ein/setup.sh It also downloads the newest images, as on any update ( Updating ). EIN_GPU=0 and ~/ein/setup.sh take the card away again. Do not edit compose.override.yaml by hand: setup.sh writes it again from .env every time it runs.

p.h: Check that EiN uses the card
p.x: Open Status under System in the sidebar. On the Overview tab, the Media service card has a GPU tile, with the card's use, its temperature and its power draw, and a VRAM used tile, with the share of its memory in use and how much of how much, each with the last six hours. Both are missing when the media service sees no card: no tile means no card, not an idle one. The card's name opens its device, /dev/ems under Devices , which keeps the same readings for a month, with the card's power limit ( The media service's machine as a device ). The GPU and VRAM tiles appear only when the media service sees a card The Media service tab shows more: Media service , at the top, names the card and its driver , and under them Graphics card says who has the card now: busy while indexing has it and search runs on the processor, quiet when there is no indexing work and search runs on the card as far as it fits, switching while it is handed over. With no card to share, or with EMS_CARD_QUIET_AFTER=0 , the mode is off and the tab leaves this out. Where the models are splits the card's memory into each model on it, the media service's own runtime, and the chat model and others , which is the language model when it shares the card; and the media service's RAM into each model there. A search model in RAM while it is also on the card is its standby copy. Under the card's bar, Media service's share sets how much of the card the media service may hold ( Share one card with the language model ). Models puts every model under what it is doing, Working , Loaded, idle , Loading or unloading or Not loaded , with its place, GPU or RAM , and size. The last 6 hours shows which models were on the card and in RAM, and when. The same is in EiN's terminal. ems-status shows every model and the device it is on, ems-status --checks the checks health reads, and ems-gpu the card's use and memory now: # in EiN's terminal ems-status --checks ems-gpu llm-status llm-status says whose the language model is and where it runs, such as http://llm:8190: ours, on the card ( reference ). It repeats what CFG_LLM_CARD says. How many of the model's layers really fit on the card is in its log ( podman compose logs llm ), which starts with the part of the card it was given and how many layers fit there, worked out at every start: llm: 6211 MB of the card, 7552 MB of it in use by others: 2548 MB left free beside the model llm: all of the model's layers fit there When they do not all fit, the second line says how many did, such as llm: 25 of the model's layers fit there; the others run on the CPU, at a fraction of the speed . To prove that every model really computes on the card, run the media service's self-test inside its container. It loads each model in turn and prints the device it bound to, ending with all GPU checks passed or a list of failures. It needs most of the card, so run it while the archive is not busy: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose exec ems python3 scripts/gpu_selftest.py --only with part of a check's name runs only the checks that match.

p.h: Share one card with the language model
p.x: With both --ems and --llm on one card, each keeps to its own part of it: The media service's share is the most of the card its models hold. A model that would take it past the share runs on the processor, even while the rest of the card is free. The language model's reserve is how much of the card the language model leaves the media service. It takes as many layers as fit in the rest when it starts, and runs the others on the processor. Set the media service's share on the Media service tab of the Status page: under the Graphics card bar in Where the models are , drag Media service's share between none and all . Under the slider, the tab says what the media service and the card's other programs hold now, and which models run on the processor at the share chosen. The share takes effect at once; the language model's reserve is set where it runs The share takes effect at once. Models that no longer fit leave the card, those at work when their work is done, and each loads next on the card or the processor as the share leaves room for it. none runs every model on the processor, and once the media service has finished the work it is doing, none of its programs holds any of the card, so nvidia-smi no longer lists them. Speech needs 4.4 GB of the share for its model on the card; with less, recordings are transcribed on the processor, at about twice their length. Transcripts already made stay as they are, wherever they were made. The slider sets CFG_EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB , and the ems-link service gives it to the media service, again after each of its restarts. The terminal sets it the same way: # in EiN's terminal config set CFG_EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB 9700 Until it is set, the media service keeps the share it starts with, from ~/ein/.env . The language model's reserve is set there too, and is read when the model starts: Variable Read by Default What it sets EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB the media service empty The share the media service starts with, in MB, until EiN's setting gives it another. Empty is the whole card, 0 none of it. LLM_CARD_RESERVE_MB the language model 8800 How much of the card the language model leaves the media service. It takes as many layers as fit in the rest, and runs the others on the processor. Set the language model's reserve 400 MB above the media service's share: the language model counts the card as nvidia-smi does, and some 400 MB of that are never usable by the media service. The media service then never loads into the language model's part. The language model fits its layers into the card less its reserve each time it starts, its restarts included, whatever the media service holds at the time, so it gets the same part whichever of the two started first. setup.sh sets neither, so the media service may use the whole card while the language model leaves it 8800 MB; set both when the two share a card. On a 16 GB card, the pair EiN's own test machine runs with leaves the media service 9.7 GB, more than the 7.3 GB its busiest work has needed, and the language model the 6.2 GB that hold all of its layers. Set the share with the slider or config set CFG_EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB 9700 , and the reserve in ~/ein/.env : # in ~/ein/.env LLM_CARD_RESERVE_MB = 10100 Apply the reserve by starting the language model again: # on the machine EiN runs on, in ~/ein podman compose up -d llm To give the language model more of the card, lower the share first, then its reserve. On a smaller card the language model gets fewer layers and answers more slowly; on an 8 GB card it runs on the processor. A language model at a hosted provider has no part of the card, so leave the share at all and the media service uses all of it. The language model covers the model itself and the hosted alternative, and Performance and sizing how memory and processor are shared.

p.h: Be told when the card goes missing
p.x: After a reboot or a driver upgrade, a card can be lost to the containers: the media service then still runs, on the processor, and the work only gets slower. To have this show as a failure instead, tell the media service that the machine has a card: # in ~/ein/.env EMS_EXPECT_GPU = 1 Apply it with podman compose up -d . While the media service sees no card, the Status page's health badge reads Needs a person , and health and ems-status --checks list: fail ems gpu this host is meant to have a card, and none is visible The same check fails, with the error, when the card's CUDA context is lost while the media service runs. Health and status explains the badge and the checks.

Without a card, or with EIN_GPU=0 , the media service and the language model run on the processor. Nothing else changes: every output is made, the same models are used, and transcripts are made on the processor at about twice the length of the recording. The media service then needs the processor and memory the installer asks for with --ems : 4 cores, 6 or more recommended, and 16 GB of memory, 32 GB recommended ( Install EiN ).

The commands are written for podman. With Docker, write docker compose where they say podman compose . What you see What to do The installer says no NVIDIA card: everything runs on the processor, more slowly The machine has no NVIDIA card, or the system does not list one. EiN works without it. The installer says an NVIDIA card is present but nvidia-smi cannot reach its driver The driver is missing or not loaded. Run nvidia-smi to see why; a reboot after installing the driver is often needed. The installer says 610 or newer is needed to encode video on the card Install a newer driver. Until then the models still use the card where they can; video is encoded on the processor. The installer says install nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18 or newer , or 1.18 or newer is needed Install or upgrade the toolkit ( Prepare the machine , step 2). The installer says but no CDI spec: sudo systemctl enable --now nvidia-cdi-refresh.service Run that command, then check that /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml exists. The installer says podman 4.9.3 rejects the CDI spec nvidia-container-toolkit 1.18.1 writes (cdiVersion 0.7.0), so the containers find no card: … Apply the fix with the command the line ends with, or upgrade podman to 5 or newer. The installer says Docker 27.5.1 passes the card through its CDI spec from 28.2 on: update Docker Upgrade Docker Engine to 28.2 or newer. Starting fails with unresolvable CDI devices nvidia.com/gpu=all The engine cannot read the CDI file. On podman before 5, apply the fix ; otherwise check that /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml exists. With Docker, check that it is Engine 28.2 or newer. The card is there but the Status page's Media service card has no GPU tile EIN_GPU in ~/ein/.env is 0 , most likely because the card or the toolkit came after the install. Give the card to EiN . After a reboot the media service does not start, or starts without the card A container keeps the device paths it was made with, and a reboot can renumber them. Make the containers again from the current CDI file: podman compose up -d --force-recreate . Models show CPU on the Media service tab while the card has room The card may be full at that moment, held by the language model, or kept from the media service by its share. Look at Where the models are and the Media service's share under it ( Share one card ). The chat answers slowly on a machine with a card The language model got only some of its layers, or none. Its log, podman compose logs llm , says how many fit on the card when it started. Raise the part of the card it gets by lowering the media service's share and LLM_CARD_RESERVE_MB together. A transcription waits for a long time While the media service's share holds whisper, it waits for about 4 GB of the card to be free rather than move to the processor. It goes on once other models are unloaded. Troubleshooting has more. The media service covers the media service beyond its card, and The language model the model beyond its card.

This page is for the administrator who wants a second machine, such as a laptop or a desktop with a card of its own, to take part of the media service's work beside the first. It applies once the media service runs. EiN uses one media service, the primary , for everything unless told otherwise. Each other media service, an instance , runs on a machine of its own, serves the operations it is set up to serve, and gets from EiN only the kinds of work whose operations it serves. Work it cannot do goes back at once to the primary, so adding an instance never holds anything up.

Each kind of work in the media pool names the media service's operations its steps call. An instance takes a kind when it serves every one of them, and when it makes their results the way the primary makes them: the same face models, picture and text embedders, text reader, way of reading damage and transcription settings. A result made otherwise would look stale to EiN, or would be a vector in another space than the ones stored, so such a kind stays with the primary. Kind Worker Operations ingest media-worker media.probe stills media-worker image.renditions , video.poster , audio.waveform , video.storyboard transcode media-worker video.transcode , audio.transcode fingerprint media-worker fingerprint.compute shots models video.shots embed-picture models vision.embed ocr models ocr.read , text.embed embed-text models text.embed transcribe models speech.transcribe , text.embed faces models faces.detect , faces.detect_video , image.renditions , video.poster diarize models speech.voiceprint , speech.active_speakers damage models image.damage restore models image.unfade , image.defects , image.inpaint , image.denoise , image.copy_tags , image.renditions The other kinds of the media pool run in EiN alone and stay with the primary. A search a person is waiting on goes to the primary too; when it does not answer, the search goes to an instance that serves the operation and makes it the way the primary did. A transcode an instance refuses for its own memory budget is not counted as refused: the primary gets it.

p.h: What a machine without a card can run
p.x: Nothing is turned off on a machine without a card: every model runs on the processor instead, only more slowly. Which operations are worth giving it is your choice, made with EMS_OPS : Operations On the processor alone media.probe , image.renditions , image.decode , video.poster , video.frames , audio.* , fingerprint.compute , document.extract , document.renditions The tools: they run on the processor on any machine. A good share for a second machine. video.transcode , video.storyboard Run, more slowly than on a card's video units; a long video beyond the machine's memory budget is refused and goes to the primary. vision.embed , text.embed , ocr.read , faces.detect Run, several times slower than on a card. Worth it on a machine that is otherwise idle. speech.transcribe , speech.voiceprint , speech.diarize , speech.active_speakers , faces.detect_video , video.shots Run, many times slower. A transcript made on the processor is made in other settings than the primary's on a card, so EiN never gives it one.

On the other machine, run the media service with its own name, its key and the operations it serves. With podman: # on the other machine podman run -d --name ems --restart always -p 8181:8181 \ --cap-add SYS_ADMIN --device /dev/fuse \ -e EMS_NAME=laptop \ -e EMS_KEY=a-long-random-key \ -e EMS_OPS= 'media.probe,image.*,video.poster,audio.*,fingerprint.compute,vision.embed' \ --memory 16g ghcr.io/einhq/ems:main Add --device nvidia.com/gpu=all on a machine with an NVIDIA card set up as The graphics card says. EMS_OPS is a list of operations separated by commas, where * stands for any part of a name; without it the instance serves everything. An operation it does not serve is answered op_not_served . Make EiN's file port reachable from the other machine. The media service reaches the files of each request through EiN's ems-files port, 2224 ( How the media service reaches your files ): with the standard install, set CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS to this machine's address and the port in ~/ein/.env , such as CFG_EMS_FILES_ADDRESS=192.168.1.10:2224 , and run ./setup.sh , which then publishes the port. On a network you do not trust, turn on CFG_EMS_FILES_TLS too. In EiN's terminal, as an administrator, add the instance with its address, its key and the address it reaches EiN's files at: # in EiN's terminal ems-instance add laptop --url http://192.168.1.20:8181 --key a-long-random-key --files-address 192.168.1.10:2224 The key is kept where only administrators read it. Without --files-address the instance reaches the files where the primary does, which another machine usually cannot. Within a minute the models and media-worker services start over with a worker for the new instance. ems-instance list shows it: main up http://ems:8181 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti fb6a7d9 laptop up http://192.168.1.20:8181 CPU only media.probe image.renditions … 1a14c9e On the other machine, raise the read-ahead of its mounts as Faster reading through the mount says, or big videos come through slowly. The instance's slots, how much EiN keeps in flight against it, are its own limits until you set them: ems-instance set laptop --model-slots 2 --cpu-slots 4 . ems-instance show laptop prints the instance with the slots in force.

The Media service tab of the Status lists the instances beside what the chosen one holds: each up or down , its card or CPU only , and the operations another serves. On a phone the list is a menu above it. The Overview tab has GPU and VRAM tiles for each instance with a card, under its name. The Work tab's Where the work is has a group for each instance, under its name, in At the media service and On a model . The health checks of an instance carry its name: ems laptop , ems laptop worker , ems laptop gpu and ems laptop card . An instance that does not answer is a warning: its work goes to the others. In the terminal, ems-status , ems-gpu and ems-models take --instance laptop ; without it they are about the primary. When an instance stops answering, its workers stop and hand back what they held; they start again when it answers. When its operations or its models change, its workers start over with the kinds it now serves, and a new build of it runs the failed work again, as a new build of the primary does.

# in EiN's terminal ems-instance set laptop --url http://192.168.1.21:8181 ems-instance remove laptop The primary is not changed with ems-instance : it is the media service the settings name, CFG_EMS_URL and CFG_EMS_KEY .

The commands the media service module adds. They are there once the module is installed. 10 of them, by name. Every command also says this with --help ; Commands explains how to read an entry. ems-files · ems-files-grant · ems-gpu · ems-instance · ems-link · ems-memory · ems-models · ems-sampler · ems-status · ems-text-embed
Serve the media service the files of its requests in flight over SFTP, the only way it reaches EiN's files (the ems-files service) administrators only · changes things ems-files

Names for paths through ems-files for a while, and the EMS-Files header that reaches them, to try a media service's way to EiN's files by hand. administrators only · changes things ems-files-grant [--read=<string>] [--write=<string>] [--seconds=<string>] Option What it does --read=<string> A file to read, as a VFS path or a path on disk; may be given more than once. --write=<string> A file to write; may be given more than once. --seconds=<string> How long the names last (default 300) ems-files-grant -- read /archive/albums/Exempelalbum_2019/IMG_0001.JPG --seconds 120 With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : the EMS-Files header value, then a line per path: read or write, its name, the path.

The GPU of an instance of the media service now, with the last six hours of utilization and VRAM, from its machine device. reads only ems-gpu [--gauge] [--instance=<string>] Option What it does --gauge The GPU and VRAM gauges top draws beside the host, each instance's with a card (the ems-sampler service declares it) --instance=<string> The instance whose card (ems-instance list); main, the primary, by default. ems-gpu ems-gpu --instance laptop ems-gpu --gauge With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : utilPct, memUsedMb, memTotalMb, tempC, vramPercent and the utilization and VRAM series, or null when there is no reading.

The media service's instances: list them and what each serves, or add, change or remove one beside the primary. administrators only · reads only ems-instance [--url=<string>] [--key=<string>] [--files-address=<string>] [--model-slots=<string>] [--cpu-slots=<string>] [--names] [--others] <action> <name> <field> Argument What it is <action> list (the default), show, add, set or remove. One of list , show , add , set , remove . <name> show, add, set, remove: the instance; main is the primary. <field> show: print this field alone (url, filesAddress, modelSlots, cpuSlots, answering, calls, ops) Option What it does --url=<string> add, set: where the instance answers, http://host:port . --key=<string> add, set: the bearer key the instance expects; empty for none. --files-address=<string> add, set: host:port of ems-files as the instance reaches it; empty for the primary's. --model-slots=<string> add, set: model requests kept in flight against it; empty for its own limit. --cpu-slots=<string> add, set: tool requests kept in flight against it; empty for its own limit. --names list: the names alone, without asking any instance. --others list: leave out the primary. ems-instance list ems-instance add laptop --url http://192.168.1.20:8181 --key let-me-in --files-address 192.168.1.10:2224 ems-instance show laptop modelSlots ems-instance set laptop --cpu-slots 2 ems-instance remove laptop With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : list: each instance with its address, files address, slots and whether a key is set, and while it answers its own name, ops, card and build. show: one, or one field of it.

Watch every instance of the media service: log when one comes or goes, run failed work again when one's build changes, and keep the primary's card at the share CFG_EMS_CARD_SHARE_MB names (the ems-link service) administrators only · changes things ems-link

The memory of the media service's machine now, with the last six hours, and what EMS holds of it. reads only ems-memory ems-memory With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : usedMb, totalMb, percent, emsMb, emsLimitMb and the series of percent, or null when there is no reading.

What the media service held over the last hours, a sample a minute, with the work EiN had waiting beside it. reads only ems-models [--hours=<string>] [--instance=<string>] Option What it does --hours=<string> Hours of history, 1 to 24 (default 6) --instance=<string> The instance (ems-instance list); main, the primary, by default. ems-models ems-models --hours 24 ems-models --instance laptop With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : windowMs and samples: at, and mode, copies, working, notStarted and inLine.

Drive the machine each instance of the media service runs on as a device, and sample what it holds (the ems-sampler service) administrators only · changes things ems-sampler service restart ems-sampler

Show media service health: version, every model and its state, what is executing, degradation, worker memory and queues. reads only ems-status [--brief] [--checks] [--instance=<string>] Option What it does --brief One line, degradation first (used by service-list --detail) --checks The checks health reads: answering, model worker, degradations, card. --instance=<string> The instance to ask (ems-instance list); main, the primary, by default, and for --checks every one.

Texts as vectors, by EMS's current text model, to compare by meaning. reads only ems-text-embed [--role=<string>] [--timeout=<number>] [--model] <text>... Argument What it is <text>... the texts, one vector each. Option What it does --role=<string> query for what is searched with, document (the default) for what is searched. --timeout=<number> seconds to wait for EMS. --model the current text model alone, no vectors. ems-text-embed --role query 'restart a service' ems-text-embed --model With JSON_OUTPUT=1 : model, the model that made them, and vectors, one per text in order.
